item_1.desc: A ring that once belonged to a powerful necromancer.
item_1.lead: The Abraxus ring is a ring that is a quest reward for completing the What Remains is Written secondary quest. Additional copies can be crafted from a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring has a chance to reduce the rune cost of utility spells when cast.

journal.text: Little is known about the great necromancer, Abraxus, a fact he finds deeply frustrating. In his youth he sought secrets forbidden to others and he wandered the Whispering Swamps of Brynmoor in search of secrets that others dared not know. The swamp was ancient and haunted, so the legends went, and there was a magic to it that was different to any other part of Ashenfall. He explored vaults, caves and battled goblins in the mists, but never found the power that his youth demanded. Until one day, he found the smoke that promised him the power he so desperately craved. From there his history is clouded, obscured just as the mist obscured the swamps. He founded a small order of necromancers in Fellhollow and took advantage of the chaos when the Withering began. He sought to bind the souls of the dead into his service, gaining power just as Imaru gained hers from the consumption of the fallen. But Abraxus was no dragon, and so frustratingly mortal. A single hoplite spear is all it took to end his life, he would have been embarrassed if he felt it had mattered. As a spirit he lost a lot of things we take for granted, sensation, corporeality, and many of the emotions that everyone else enjoys. Yet, in exchange, he was given the most precious gift of all – time. Time to contemplate. Time to scheme. Time to think about what really matters, in the grand scheme of it all, and he has found his answer. His ring, imbued with his dark power, offers no value to him any more. So he bequeaths it to you. In time, perhaps, it may help you become a mage strong enough to earn his respect. Well, a small fraction of it, at least.

item_2.desc: A durable adamant helmet forged for the strongest of warriors.
item_2.lead: Adamant helmet is a power level 7 armour piece.

journal.text: It was the dwarves who first discovered adamant: a metal so strong and powerful that it could turn aside almost any other blade. It was hard to work with and difficult to refine, so it saw little use in the early ages. Malgo, druid of Guthix, was one of the first to see the worth in adamant. It was an age before dwarves were cursed by Zamorak to be unable to use magic without severe consequence, and Malgo was one of the greatest spellcasters of his people. He joined the ranks of the Guthixian druids, even though - like many dwarves - he was only a follower of Guthix, rather than a worshipper.

item_3.desc: A sturdy set of adamant chest armour, forged for the strongest of warriors.
item_3.lead: Adamant platebody is a power level 7 armour piece.

journal.text: It was the dwarves who first discovered adamant: a metal so strong and powerful that it could turn aside almost any other blade. It was hard to work with and difficult to refine, so it saw little use in the early ages. As Malgo and his expedition headed into the deserts of Ashenfall, they found wonderous new ores, materials and treasures that promised to expand their knowledge and understanding by leagues. They also found Karibdos, the devourer. It was a great beast that lay within the sands; some dread creature that should never have existed. It was buried beneath the region, massive and hungry and, as the expedition approached, it opened wide its maw and attempted to swallow the entire group whole. With quick thinking and forgotten spells, Malgo summoned vines for the expedition members to grasp. Many failed and were consumed by the great vortex in the sand that was Karibdos. Though they struck back, their arrows and spells were too weak to pierce its hide and Karibdos simply returned to its slumber, waiting for the expedition to cross its path again.

item_4.desc: A sturdy set of adamant leg armour, forged for the strongest of warriors.
item_4.lead: Adamant platelegs are a power level 7 armour piece.

journal.text: It was the dwarves who first discovered adamant: a metal so strong and powerful that it could turn aside almost any other blade. It was hard to work with and difficult to refine, so it saw little use in the early ages. Karibdos was the obstacle between the rest of Ashenfall and a slow, defeated, trudge home. Malgo refused to allow the latter. He studied adamant carefully, experimenting with techniques and styles none bothered with before, even infusing it with a little magic. In doing so, he discovered the strength of the material. When the expedition faced Karibdos again, it was in suits of solid adamant and glistening green blades ready to strike. They fell into the beast’s great maw, but rather than a delicious dwarven meal, Karibdos found its teeth shattering against their armour and its ancient hide torn apart from flashing blades of green metal. With Karibdos dead and gone, Malgo and his team continued deeper into the region, vanishing into legend. For those who make the desert their home, none have witnessed anything like Karibdos again… though, perhaps, they simply haven’t dug deep enough.

journal.text: You brought simple cloth trousers with you from the mainland. They barely qualify as armour, but they’re better than no armour at all. These clothes have seen you across the oceans, keeping you warm in the cold sea breeze. Now starched with sea salt and weathered by labouring away on the ship deck, these clothes are a testament to how far you’ve come. This is the furthest you’ve ever been from home, and perhaps it’s a chance to craft a new one.

item_6.desc: Basic and comfortable attire fit for a new adventurer.
item_6.lead: Adventurer's tunic is a basic item that can be crafted using 9 coarse animal fur at the crafting table.

journal.text: A simple tunic brought with you from the mainland. It barely classes as armour, but it’s better than no armour at all. When you joined the expedition, you had nothing but the clothes on your back. All your worldly belongings were lost, and all your gold drained away. Debt collectors would appear out of the shadows, swarming toward you like rats seeking cheese. What choice did you have but to leave? The expedition offered you a chance away from all your troubles. An opportunity to escape the cruel hand that fate has dealt you. These clothes once represented everything you ever lost, but now they represent the threadbare start of a new beginning.

item_7.desc: Congratulations! Reaching level 99 in Agility is an astonishing feat. Wear this cape with pride.
item_7.lead: The Agility cape is a Cape of Accomplishment able to be crafted and worn with a level 99 Agility. It can be crafted at the crafting table. This cape, while worn, gives the player a small chance to not consume stamina for jumping, dashing, or evading.

item_9.lead: The amulet of accuracy is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the amulet grants players a 15% increase in critical damage and critical weakpoint damage.

journal.text: The Wild Knights knew the dangers of missing their target. If an arrow did not slay its target quickly, then too soon would the quarry either escape, or, worse, gather friends. Wolf packs could easily tear a small group of Knights to pieces if not dealt with fast. The Amulet of Accuracy made sure that hunts went smoothly. When a shot landed, it landed hard. Alpha wolves would be slain in a single well-placed shot, and sturdier threats might go down in a small flurry of arrows. When Silverthorn Keep stood against the rising horde of zombies, these amulets were worn by the keep defenders who unleashed a torrent of arrows into the hungry dead.

item_10.desc: A mystical amulet that strengthens your defences.
item_10.lead: The amulet of defence is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the amulet increases players' armour Value of all three damage types by 5 for each piece (head, torso, and legs).

journal.text: Not everyone can wear armour when faced with the hordes of shambling undead. Children and the frail, become targets with little to protect them from gnashing teeth and jaws. In these scenarios magic becomes incredibly important, and these amulets delayed the deaths of countless lives. Not everyone was happy with such utilitarian approaches to survival, however. As the days drew on and resources grew scarce, empathy began to wane in the population of Emberwood. Amulets of defence were handed out to those determined to have the most need, but the criteria for that became a hot subject of contention. It would be nice to imagine a world where everyone pulled together to defend against the undead, but human nature sadly shattered that dream. Still, while there would always be those who would attempt to steal the amulets from the needy, there were plenty more who would stand against them. These amulets now carry an echo of those protectors, shielding its wearers from harm.

item_11.lead: The amulet of glory is an amulet that boosts melee, magic, and ranged critical damage while also increasing defence. While worn, the amulet provides an additional +5 defence to all combat styles and 25% increase to magical attacks, melee attacks, and ranged critical damage.

journal.text: Power, trapped in dragonstone crystal and worn around the neck, that is the essence of this amulet. The facets of the dragonstone refract and refine the enchantments cast upon the item, somehow creating a magical lattice of surprising strength. Many have tried to create variations of this theme, yet dragonstone proves too fragile a substance for practical use. Once someone attempted to make a dragonstone dagger, to see if they could turn it into a blade of glory, yet they could not find a sufficiently large stone that wasn't valuable enough to bankrupt a small nation. One wizard attempted strange alchemical practices to try and forge a staff of pure dragonstone. Alas, not only did he fail to create such a stone, but the magical explosion that resulted from his hubris removed his lab, and all his research, from this plane of reality. It's probably a good idea that no one attempted to duplicate his work.

item_12.lead: The amulet of Magic is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the amulet grants players increased magic damage by a factor of 12.5%. The recipe is unlocked through Death's Exchange for 350 soul fragments.

journal.text: Emberwood had its fair share of spellcasters, though lacking the funding of the tower to the south. With more limited resources the mages of Emberwood found other methods to strengthen their art, and the Amulet of Magic was popular among all of them. Druids worse{{sic|incorrectly spelled "wore" in cache

item_13.lead: The amulet of strength is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the amulet increases the player's melee damage with both one-handed and two-handed weapons by 12.5% each.

journal.text: Might makes right, is the cry of every wannabe despot. Bandos in particular was very fond of this statement. This amulet upholds that notion and does its best to help make sure you are the most correct person around. It imbues your muscles with body-aligned anima, the magic strengthening the sinew and fortifying your bones. It adds greater force to your swing that will crush your enemies before you. The goblin general, Snotknucke, wore this amulet and attempted to hunt down Velgar. He believed that, with its magic, he could fell the beast in a single swing of his club. Snotknuckle was stronger, deadlier and more powerful than ever, but this did very little against the rock that Velgar dropped on his head.

journal.text: Ava is the apprentice to Dr Oddenstein, an eccentric scientist who lives in Draynor Manor, and a skilled inventor in her own right. She whiles away her limited free time by studying the lesser-known field of necroballistics, and creating strange and wonderful gizmos to further her studies. Perhaps her proudest achievement, is the invention of the attractor. By harnessing the energies of an undead chicken to the harmonic frequencies of a common bar magnet, her device can snatch grounded projectiles and bring them back to the quiver before they can be lost. This money saving experiment is not only great for hunters, but for anyone looking for an excuse to fill their enemies full of sharp sticks of wood. Always the generous sort, but one with little head for marketing, Ava has decided to pass on her genius invention to others. Rather than publishing a paper, or passing the methodology onto the Varrock library, she has instead written the instructions in a bottle and sent it adrift in the ocean for anyone to find. Fate, she believes, will draw it to where it is meant to go. Like magnets, probably.

journal.text: Blue dragons are not native to Dowdun Reach, because blue dragons are not native anywhere. They are creations of the dragonkin, and this particular strain is Lacrussa's work. Lacrussa did not consider them failures, but she did not consider them successes, either. They were stepping stones: and, as such, she let them rest on Dowdun Reach. Rasthin changed everything. She came to Avisk with a gift: 'Jas Moksha', in the tongue of the Kin. It was a device that imbued Avisk with the element of air. Avisk accepted the gift politely. Rasthin could have over-powered him with ease. He played supplicant and took the gift, hoping that it wasn't a trap or curse. That disdain shifted once Avisk realised that the powers were not limited to the material realm. He could move with alacrity, purpose and strength in the minds of others. Minds that were once closed to him blossomed like a flower. He dabbled with ogres, and then moved on to blue dragons. Within the minds of blue dragons, he found a secret. There was a blockage - a multi-faceted prism - that kept their potential at bay. It redirected their thoughts in wild directions, made them unruly. It seemed that their animalistic nature was a product of mental hindrances, rather than physical. With his new powers, he could solve a problem that had hounded Lacrussa for centuries.

journal.text: Blue dragons are not native to Dowdun Reach, because blue dragons are not native anywhere. They are creations of the dragonkin, and this particular strain is Lacrussa's work. Lacrussa did not consider them failures, but she did not consider them successes, either. They were stepping stones: and, as such, she let them rest on Dowdun Reach. Avisk maneuvered the multi-faceted prism within the blue dragon's mind. He observed it using his mastery of air, but no permutation would focus the blue dragon's thoughts, no orientation would align the chaos. He resolved to break parts of that giant stone, but its power was diminished with each snap and shatter. He crumpled to the floor of the blue dragon's mind-space in frustration. The breakthrough was borne from that frustration. Just as he would move into the consciousness of a living being, he moved into the consciousness of the stone. Perhaps he forgot where he was. Against all his expectations, he was able to step into the stone itself, as if it itself had a consciousness. There was a second layer to the blue dragon's mind. It is impossible to comprehend what Avisk saw there. But he was forever changed. He no longer cared for healing the blue dragons of their crystalline blockage, of restoring them to sapient thought. Instead, he wished to recreate the prism, the crystal, in the corporeal world.

journal.text: Blue dragons are not native to Dowdun Reach, because blue dragons are not native anywhere. They are creations of the dragonkin, and this particular strain is Lacrussa's work. Lacrussa did not consider them failures, but she did not consider them successes, either. They were stepping stones: and, as such, she let them rest on Dowdun Reach. Avisk initially had no use for them. His focus was on lower species, humans and the like. He saw room within human minds to crawl and make them his own. Their consciousness was a hall of prisms, and he could turn them all so that they focused on him. The human mind reflected back his narcissism. To Avisk, the blue dragons were nuisances, liable to kill his test subjects while he was distracted. He penned them and forgot about them, cursing Lacrussa for letting them stray into his domain. Their number grew, but Avisk tutted and continued his work.

journal.text: The desert is a cruel and unforgiving place, and that was before Fuzan corrupted the sun against it. Dry air, filled with sand particles, leech all moisture from the body, leaving you dehydrated, exhausted and with no respite in view. Oases can be mirages, tricks played by the dunes to lure you deeper into your own destruction. These robes help to limit some of the desert’s power, through ancient tricks learned by those who have dwelled within the dunes for generations. The hood is the most basic necessity of the desert. It shields the top of one’s head from the sun’s cruel ministrations, acting as a barrier between sunstroke and you. The hood also helps protect against particulates of sand that have been stirred up by meagre breezes. The overhanging fabric shields the eyes from the light, just a little. A tiny point of shade in a glaring light that’s almost crushing in its brightness. Finally, they’re surprisingly fashionable, everyone should try one.

journal.text: The desert is a cruel and unforgiving place, and that was before Fuzan corrupted the sun against it. Dry air, filled with sand particles, leech all moisture from the body, leaving you dehydrated, exhausted and with no respite in view. Oases can be mirages, tricks played by the dunes to lure you deeper into your own destruction. These robes help to limit some of the desert’s power, through ancient tricks learned by those who have dwelled within the dunes for generations. These simple leggings are all that stands between you and obliteration by a sandstorm. Sand can be sharp, it can be abrasive and, given time, it can wear a person down to nothing but the memory of them in another person’s mind. Cloth won’t stop that, not really, but it will delay the obliteration long enough for you to get to shelter when the worst of the storm hits. You’ll still want to run, though.

journal.text: Those joining the Fellhollow military who were not from the more noble bloodlines would go into the force known as hoplites. This force of warrior farmers named themselves after the hoplites of Hallow, legendary forces spoken of in some of the Saradominist text. These hoplites would meet at the end of each week to train and practice battle manoeuvres. They became walls of impenetrable shields, or terrifying spiked shells, moving with the sort of unity that only comes over years and years of training. Their secret, so they claimed, was the weekly barbeque. Once training was resolved, if they had performed well enough, the retired members of the hoplites would cook them delicious meats and roasted vegetables, served with an overly generous helping of alcoholic beverages.

As their members fell, they would rise as the undead and immediately turn on their brethren, ripping the group apart from the inside. At least in death they stand together again.

journal.text: Wear the skin of your enemies, so that they know to fear you! This is the ranger way, to dress themselves in the outer layers of weaker dragons so that they larger dragons know not to mess with them. Love makes fools of all of us. Infatuation more so, especially one-sided. Bilar was in love, so he claimed. He spoke of her beauty. He spoke of her acumen. He spoke of… well, he spoke a lot about things that you do not repeat in polite society. He wanted her and he wanted the ultimate gift to win her affection: a dragon’s heart. Yet, dragons are unwilling to part with such a vital organ, and Bilar had to get creative. He found a dead dragon, one that had been slain in battle with a rival, and he decided to skin it. With it’s scaley hide in his possession he spent weeks fashioning powerful armour from the remains, until he had an outfit that resembled the creature he hunted. So dressed, he set out towards the great stone circle near Emberwood, knowing that a dragon had recently made it its home. He would slay it, claim its heart and present it to the woman he loved and she would surely agree to be his forever.

item_85.desc: Agile Ranged leg armour crafted from Green Dragonhide.

journal.text: Wear the skin of your enemies, so that they know to fear you! This is the ranger way, to dress themselves in the outer layers of weaker dragons so that they larger dragons know not to mess with them. The funeral of Bilar Amaris was not a particularly popular one. A few fellow hunters stopped by to pay the briefest of respects, and a drunk great uncle turned up and got the name wrong. His death would have passed into complete obscurity, except for the clothes he was wearing when he died. Despite the mauled condition of his corpse, the villagers that found him noticed the surprisingly supple and yet sturdy armour. Barely a scratch covered the dragonhide, and they remarked that if only he’d covered the neck a bit better, then he might not have ended up in the state he did. The villagers brought the armour back and leatherworkers set to work on repeating it and improving it. Soon the best hunters in Emberwood would be wearing green dragonhide armour, and matched with better common sense, it kept them alive much longer.

journal.text: Wear the skin of your enemies, so that they know to fear you! This is the ranger way, to dress themselves in the outer layers of weaker dragons so that they larger dragons know not to mess with them. Such was the logic of Bilar Amaris, a hunter that dwelled withing Emberwood. He was renowned among the locals, skilled with the bow and capable of taking down almost any prey. When the green dragons descended on the region, he decided that he would be the apex predator, hunting them down. This was partially done in a misguided attempt to win the affections of the “black-haired beauty” that had set up a little potion shop in the village. Like many idiots, he had convinced himself that all a woman could ever want was a strong man that was capable of killing something bigger than he was. He was, unsurprisingly, deeply mistaken.

journal.text: While the Ashenfall gyrhawk is long-extinct, it lives on as a symbol. The form of the gyrhawk was adopted by anyone who want to convey a sense of speed. Gyrhawk Postal Services were popular in happier times around Brynmoor, while the Gyrhawk Swimmers were the ones to beat in swimming galas. Perhaps the most common use of an Ashenfall Gyrhawk's form was on medals and amulets, given to the winners of athletic competitions. Gilded gyrhawk amulets were given for first place, while second and third received ungilded. The amulets weren't worn in the heats themselves - that would be decidedly unfair, since they give performance benefits - but seeing a gyrhawk amulet around someone's neck was a good indicator that they were the athletic type.

journal.text: Garou druids borrow from nature when crafting staves or weaving robes. In Ghornfell they took antlers from deer, and leather from their hunted prey. In the Umbral Sands they were forced to adopt a… sparklier approach. Parts of the kalphites, most notably their wings, were a scintillating spectrum of beautiful colours. As they caught the sunlight, they would bloom into a radiant rainbow of delight and Karia found herself overcome with a strange sort of envy previously unknown to her people. She wanted to sparkle. She wanted to shine. She wanted to live a life encased in the most magnificent and wondrous colours, and she would do anything to make it happen. To call the events that followed a war would be an over-exaggeration, but not wholly inaccurate. The garou descended on the hives with blade, claw and bow, ready to tear the beasts apart so that they might claim the colourful materials for themselves. The kalphite, of course, did not fall easily and many garou lives were lost in the clothing-mad conflict.

journal.text: Garou druids borrow from nature when crafting staves or weaving robes. In Ghornfell, they took antlers from deer, and leather from their hunted prey. In the Umbral Sands they were forced to adopt a… sparklier approach. Kaira, druid of the Softfoot tribe, was one of the first of the Moon Garou to hunt through the sands in search of materials they could use to craft robes of their own. They expected magnificent beasts with scales and horns the likes of which they had never seen. They found the kalphites instead. Their first interaction did not go well.

item_95.desc: A wizard's hat, infused with boundless magical power.

journal.text: Garou druids borrow from nature when crafting staves or weaving robes. In Ghornfell they took antlers from deer, and leather from their hunted prey. In the Umbral Sands they were forced to adopt a… sparklier approach. The kalphite did not offer diplomatic solutions to the garou’s assaults, but they offered violent ones. On one night, the garou saw an approaching sandstorm, but were not prepared for the truth. As the storm approached, the buzzing sound grew to a crescendo as the great kalphite swarm blotted out the stars and moon, descending upon the village. There were none left alive once all had passed. You would think this would have been the end of it, that death and pain would be deterrent enough. Yet, for the years, decades and centuries that followed, the desire for colourful material was too strong a lure. Countless lives have been lost to kalphite retribution. But what is fashion without a little sacrifice?

item_96.lead: The inspiring amulet of Attack is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants players an additional 5% Attack experience while working with the skill.

journal.text: Magic lives in the dirt, the ore and the rocks. It crystallises inside gemstones, matrices of magical energy just waiting to be unlocked. In Brynmoor the priests of Saradomin kept the secrets of magical amulets within their purview. They would craft jewellery that would enhance the fighting instinct of their soldiers, and hand then{{sic|incorrectly spelled "them"

item_97.lead: The inspiring amulet of Magic is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the amulet grants players an additional 5% Magic experience while working with the skill.

journal.text: It is perhaps not surprising that wizard’s made use of magical jewellery as early as possible. Indeed the first few pieces worn on Ashenfall were little more than decoration, and gaudy wizards would attempt to outdo one another with shinier and shinier pieces. As part of their ever increasing “prank war” wizards began to create jewellery that was enchanted with effects designed to frustrate, or otherwise hinder, the wearer, believing that enchantments in jewellery were little more than silly trinkets. One mage created what she assumed was an auditory illusion, within an amulet, the intention being that when the wearer would try and cast a spell, the jewellery would play an annoying earworm tune, distracting the poor caster. This did not happen. Something about the threads of magic, the structure of the crystal and the concealing spell that was intended to hide the prank, created something unique. Instead of making it harder to cast spell, the wearers found it easier. Understanding came faster, spells and incantations clearer than before. What was intended to distract instead focused the wearer, allowing them to concentrate in ways they had never been able to before.

item_98.lead: The inspiring amulet of Ranged is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants players an additional 5% Ranged experience while working with the skill.

journal.text: The Wild Knights used many tools and tricks in their hunts. Looking for any edge they might have against the untamed wilds of Ashenfall. One jeweller, a water-Amalgamated by the name of Lochlan, created an amulet imbued with the communal spirit of the hunters. He would leave the gemstone, that would serve as its base, in the gathering hall and soon it became a tradition for each hunter to touch the gemstone if their hunt was successful. Over the years this gemstone took on their pride, prowess and skill and that became a magical enchantment that lay within the heart of the stone. Crafting an amulet from the crystal, Lochlan found a way of sharing that enchantment with everyone who wore it. Now, millennia later, the echoes of that enchantment linger within the crystals, just waiting for someone to remember them.

item_99.lead: The inspiring ring of Agility is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants players an additional 5% Agility experience while training.

item_100.lead: The inspiring ring of Artisan is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants players an additional 5% Artisan experience while working with the skill.

journal.text: No one quite knows why this ring works. It's as if ancestral grandmothers hover behind the wearer, whispering to them the ancient secrets of their crafting techniques. Old styles, long since lost to tragedy or history, can be restored in a flash of inspiration when someone wears this amulet. But most wearers simply find themselves in a trance-like state - able to ignore the world around them and focus their craft. Learning more and more about it with each moment that passes.

item_101.lead: The inspiring ring of Construction is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants the players an additional 5% Construction experience while working with the skill.

journal.text: This ring is infused with tiny elements of the dragonkin Brakka, a powerful creature and an architect of some skill. His hubris remains, even after his death at Kuldra's hands, and motes of his knowledge can be preserved within crystalline structures. Although you cannot glean the secrets of the dragonkin from these motes of memory, his instinct and innate talent for construction can be harnessed to create a ring that simplifies understanding the art of architecture.

item_102.lead: The inspiring ring of Cooking is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants the players an additional 5% Cooking experience while working with the skill.

journal.text: Cooking is a form of magic that few people truly master. Meals can return lost memories, shatter sour moods, and rekindle friendships long since abandoned. This ring was created by accident, when a parent was trying to teach a child how to cook. They were holding the unfinished piece absent-mindedly, as they explained to their progeny about all the steps needed to understand a recipe. This knowledge, infused with the emotion of a parent's instruction, enchanted the ring so that all future wearers might benefit from their knowledge.

item_103.lead: The inspiring ring of Farming is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants players an additional 5% Farming experience while working with the skill.

item_104.lead: The inspiring ring of Fishing is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants players an additional 5% Fishing experience while working with the skill.

item_105.lead: The inspiring ring of Mining is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants players an additional 5% Mining experience while working with the skill.

journal.text: The dwarves know that the earth has a memory, gemstones especially so. What they don't tell you is that the earth holds a grudge. Each time a pick pierces the stone or smashes a piece of ore from its home, the earth remembers. A skilled enchanter can use that grudge, that earthen memory, and turn it back against the bitter earth. Traditionally this is done via jewellery, with dwarven goldsmiths making most of their living from miners purchasing these trinkets.

item_106.lead: The inspiring ring of Runecrafting is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants players an additional 5% Runecrafting experience while working with the skill.

journal.text: Ashenfall was the first place where Guthix created runes, but he never passed those secrets on to his followers. Only when the legendary human, V, discovered the secret was it taught to the general population. Still, something about Ashenfall makes the process easier. No altars are needed, nor talismans required, yet runes can be crafted with an abundance that would make mainland guilds jealous. This ring taps into that ease, infusing the soul with some of that ancient knowledge of the island. Be careful sleeping with this on, as you may dream the memories of runecrafters past. Or of a dog made of cheese. No one knows why.

item_107.lead: The inspiring ring of Woodcutting is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants players an additional 5% Woodcutting experience while working with the skill.

journal.text: If trees could move, they would kill us all. That's the terrible truth that no lumberjack speaks of, instead they silently protect the rest of us from arboreal wrath. When a lumberjack was trained by the druids in Brynmoor, and taught the secrets of the murderous woods, they would be gifted a ring to help them in their battle against the vile trees. These trinkets have helped lumberjacks defend us all from the cruelty of the woods, in a war that most don't even believe is happening.

item_111.lead: Kalphite carapace chest is a power level 7 ranged armour that can be crafted at an armour bench. The recipe is unlocked by purchasing and using the chitinous carapace vestige from Iasadair - The Merchant.

journal.text: Perhaps it’s a little strange to wear the skin of your enemy, but who am I to judge? The Kalphite are certainly an imposing bunch and donning armour comprising of the most resilient parts of them certainly hits that survival game vibe, even if it is a little grim. The shell of a Kalphite is strong and durable, a thick layer between them and the rest of the world. It keeps them safe, yes, but closed off from sensation and feeling, an emotional gulf between them and everyone else. Fortunately, they’re insects and couldn’t care any less. You, at least, are in possession of vocal chords and the ability to interact with others. You can also take off your armour, should you ever need to—something not recommended in the middle of battle, no matter how much you’d like to improve your emotional bond with something. It is worth noting, however, that there is an unexpected side effect to this armour. Dragons find you extra crunchy.

item_112.desc: This helmet is made from parts of the kalphites. Its durable but flexible nature makes it excellent for rangers
item_112.lead: Kalphite carapace helmet is a power level 7 ranged armour that can be crafted at an armour bench. The recipe is unlocked by purchasing and using the twtiching antenna vestige from Iasadair - The Merchant.

journal.text: Perhaps it’s a little strange to wear the skin of your enemy, but who am I to judge? The Kalphite are certainly an imposing bunch and donning armour comprising of the most resilient parts of them certainly hits that survival game vibe, even if it is a little grim. Once you hollow out the squishy parts of the Kalphite and rearrange the plates to better fit the human form, the carapace helmet is more comfortable than it might first seem. Seen through the eyes of the Kalphite the world is a fractured place. Multifaceted eyes see the world in strange and wonderful ways, their vision split among multiple different views, yet never obsessing over a singular image. You lose the finest details to focus on the bigger picture, a trait perhaps more of us need in our lives.

item_113.lead: Kalphite carapace legs is a power level 7 ranged armour that can be crafted at an armour bench. The recipe is unlocked by purchasing and using the barbed appendage vestige from Iasadair - The Merchant.

journal.text: Perhaps it’s a little strange to wear the skin of your enemy, but who am I to judge? The Kalphite are certainly an imposing bunch and donning armour comprising of the most resilient parts of them certainly hits that survival game vibe, even if it is a little grim. Fortunately, donning this leg armour does not change your legs into multiple skittering appendages. Aside from being deeply sinister, the animation team would murder me. Kalphites are well adapted to the sands, they spread their weight out across all six legs, allowing them to move across the sands with relative ease. They can move fast too, something Moon Garou hunters discover all too late.

journal.text: Garou magic is not born of runes, but of their connection to the moon, the stars and the spirits within them. Moon Garou shamans dance in the moonlight, with the glittering moon sprites swirling around them in mystical threads that help to reshape reality. Magic is sacred, spiritual and serene. Shamans wears these robes so that the tribe may know to call on them for spiritual aid, both magical and personal, as the shamans act as counsel as much as magician. A Moon Garou shaman must walk the deserts before they can be truly considered magi in their own right. They wander, explore and contemplate the loneliness of the sands as they do so. Some hear voices, believing them to be ancestors, deities, spirits or just their own internal monologue trying to dull the silence. Others find a profound calm in the silence, many choosing to live a quiet life in return. Others, find monsters. There are many shamans who report that they did battle with the terrible demons creeping out from Dowdun Reach. Others battled kalphites, KotHaar or even dragons. One claims to have battled a creature that rose out of smoke, whimpering and wailing as it went, and it left the shaman’s mind shattered in return. Yet, no matter how far the shamans wander, eventually they all found their way home, enlightened and enriched, and ready to serve their people.

item_121.desc: Robes woven under the light of a full moon, imbued with the wild power of the garou. Suitable for magic users, enhancing healing abilities at night.
item_121.lead: Lunar Garou robes are a power level 7 magic armour that can be crafted at an armour bench. The recipe is unlocked by purchasing and using the lunate shawl vestige from Domri - The Merchant.

journal.text: Garou magic is not born of runes, but of their connection to the moon, the stars and the spirits within them. Moon Garou shamans dance in the moonlight, with the glittering moon sprites swirling around them in mystical threads that help to reshape reality. Magic is sacred, spiritual and serene. Shamans wears these robes so that the tribe may know to call on them for spiritual aid, both magical and personal, as the shamans act as counsel as much as magician. These robes are only given to a shaman after completing three mystic trials. The first is a trial of contemplation, where each applicant is given a complicated riddle to solve and three nights in which to do so. During that time they are allowed no forms of communication, and must rely purely on their ability to contemplate the words and arrive at a solution. The answers to the riddle are rarely set in stone: it is the interpretation that matters. The second is a trial of compassion, and they are never warned of this one in advance. Indeed the trial may have happened before the applicant even entered into training. They could be tested at any point in their lives. It’s a simple trial: the applicant at some point finds someone in need and how they go about helping, or not helping them, is noted for the trial. This weeds out the cruel people pretending to be shamans, and encourages an attitude of compassion in potential applicants. The final trial is the hardest of all, the trial of creativity. Here the applicants are given time to study magic, its forms, its methods and its malleability. To complete this trial, the applicant must create a new spell, enchantment or other form of magic, that has never been seen before. This trial has led to some of the most beautiful discoveries… and some of the most terrifying.

journal.text: Although the name may be sinister, the robes and the people who wear them are not automatically evil. Brynmoor had a string of so-called “dark wizards.” Most were little more than bandits with a penchant for magic. The guards were enough to deal with most troublemakers, but a small group of them caused real trouble.They were members of the “Children of Shadows”, a Zamorakian cult that began to spread through the population. The cult fed on distrust, paranoia and greed, some very human traits. Among this number were three apprentices of the wizard’s guild, who were frustrated that they were not given the promotions they felt they deserved. In their quest for power, the ‘Children of Shadows’ stumbled upon ancient vaults, repositories of the dragonkin’s long-forgotten secrets. Here, they discovered the remnants of a forbidden text, a relic of immense power. Driven by their arrogance, they chose to follow its instructions, unaware of the horrors they were about to unleash.

journal.text: The KotHaar do not die as we do. There is no afterlife for them, just silence. They are reduced to fragments of obsidian, crushed down and down with the weight of their souls. Once returned to the Elder Kiln the KotHaar will live again, it just may take some time. Fortunately, time is irrelevant to the KotHaar and they are content to simply wait out the aeons until their time comes again. So, in a way, you do them a favour by wearing this obsidian armour, as it gives them a chance to see the world as they wait. There is a common misconception that the KotHaar are a hive mind. Certainly many of them work as if they are one, but they are bound by a shared purpose, not a shared consciousness. This is a distinction that other races struggle with regularly, but it is easily understood when, as inevitably happens once in a while, one of the KotHaar turns away from their intended purpose and dares to wonder what else could be. There are a few stories, hidden in the deserts, of KotHaar explorers found doing various things. They might spend days staring at a cactus, or they might dig through a mountainside to see what’s inside. Perhaps this chest armour, that you now wear, might once have dreamed of being something other than its purpose. Now, perhaps, that dream has come true.

item_137.lead: Obsidian helmet is a power level 7 melee armour that can be crafted at an armour bench. The vestige, chipped obsidian construct, is sold by Beartach - The Merchant.

So, in a way, you do them a favour by wearing this obsidian armour, as it gives them a chance to see the world as they wait. This helmet is durable, powerful and undeniably shiny. The obsidian glass reflects light in strange ways, glinting in a way that seems strange for such a dark material. Moon Garou that prevail against the KotHaar do not wear the obsidian as armour, despite the obvious advantages. They worry that should they don the black glass, then they will find themselves possessed by whatever fire spirit animates the KotHaar, and the Moon Garou legends of fiery beings are not their happiest stories.

Sturdy, strong and durable, these legs feel like they could wade through lava, and many have attempted to do so. Whether it worked well, none can say, because none who tried have managed to record their findings. Perhaps give it a try? What could go wrong?

journal.text: The knights of Saradomin had many names over the years. White Knights. Temple Knights. In Ashenfall, they were called Paladins. Brave and faithful, members of noble families who took up the sword. They were the second, third and fourth children of Brynmoor’s “nobility” – a title given to those families that were most loyal to the priesthood, and the most obedient were raised the highest. These platelegs were exceptionally well made. Sturdier and stronger than the armour worn by Brynmoor guards and other Ashenfall human soldiers. It was certainly stronger than the helms of the Guthixian-aligned knights or the druids they guarded. Paladins were a righteous force, noble and true to the priests' teachings. They brought order from chaos and discipline to indolence, remaking Bramblemead according to the church’s designs.

journal.text: Hate can be a powerful tool. It forges and it destroys with equal might. Grudges can last generations, well beyond the lifespans of those first slighted, and vengeance… vengeance can be eternal. Ravanna knew this well. She stoked her hatred and turned it into a weapon. She wrapped it around her soul like a cage and unleashed the power of it into the very sky over the Highlands. A storm, driven by grief, rage and unfettered loathing, turned the clouds into agents of her vengeance and as they writhe, rage and hate, they build static charge that they unleash upon the garou that live below. This ring was on her finger when Ulv died, and it became infused with that same hatred. At first it only turned its rage against the garou, but the problem with hate is that it festers and mutates into something worse. Everything is to blame for Ulv’s death. Every plant, every rock, every movement of the stars, they all led up to that moment and so the ring hates them too, and now it seeks, in its own small way, to take revenge upon the world.

journal.text: A garou hunter called Mayev was the first in Ashenfall to wear the skin of a red dragon, though she did so not out of malice, but in respect for a dear friend. To the garou, the hide of a slain foe is a mark of great pride, and the bones of a warrior are worn with great honour. Dragons are not pets. They’re violent creatures, prone to random acts of aggression, driven by a rage that burns in their very soul. Still, Mayev was patient and she lured the dragon hatchling away from the corpse of its parent and out into the desert sands. Moonlight transformed the desert from gold to glittering silver, yet the ruby-red scales of the dragon seemed brighter than before. Over the days, weeks and months to come, she kept the dragon secret. She brought it scraps of food, and kept it company on lonely days, and it came to see her not as a parent, not as a master, but as a friend. She saw him as the same. She named him Vakar – the flame-wrought song – and they would hunt together. Over time, they knew each other’s strengths and could balance out their weaknesses. They hunted stronger prey, earning the respect of her tribe with the offcuts. Life was set to be everything they had both dreamed – until they met the KotHaar, and it all turned to ash.

item_161.lead: Red dragon helmet is a power level 7 ranged armour that can be crafted at an armour bench

journal.text: A moon garou hunter called Mayev was the first in Ashenfall to wear the skin of a red dragon, though she did so not out of malice, but in respect for a dear friend. To the garou, the hide of a slain foe is a mark of great pride, and the bones of a warrior are worn with great honour. As a cub, Mayev was never one to stay in one place. She ran round and round the caravans without a care in the world, always bringing the frustration and ire of her elder. “Be still!” were the words she heard first thing in the morning. “Be quiet!” the command she heard each night before bed. Yet, stillness and silence were as alien a concept to her as the magic of the druids - something far out of her reach. One day, she left her camp in search of wild adventure, much to the chagrin of the camp guards. She risked the harsh sunlight of the dunes, clinging to shadows, exploring caves and passages revealed by the passing sandstorm of the day. Each morning her world was different, new paths appeared while familiar ones were hidden, and on this day she found a cavern deep underground. There she found a red dragon, breathing her last breath, and the hatchling beside her breathing his first.

item_162.lead: Red dragon legs are a power level 7 ranged armour that can be crafted at an armour bench

journal.text: A garou hunter called Mayev was the first in Ashenfall to wear the skin of a red dragon, though she did so not out of malice, but in respect for a dear friend. To the garou, the hide of a slain foe is a mark of great pride, and the bones of a warrior are worn with great honour. Dragonfire was little concern to creatures birthed in lava, and garou arrows bounced harmlessly off obsidian flesh. Yet, despite all this, it was the madness in their eyes that terrified Mayev the most: as if something else stared back at her. Something bright, radiating a heat greater than the sun and it took every ounce of willpower not to fall to her knees in worship. Yet, she was prey now. The hunter became the hunted and the KotHaar fell on Mayev and her dragon before she could ready a defence. She fought bravely, desperately, but it would not save her and she readied herself for a death that never came. Vakar dived into the fray, grasping her in jaws that could have severed her in two as easy as breathing. He carried her to safety. When she came to, she saw the spears, blades and shards of obisidian pressed deep into her friend and she held him in his last breaths, thanking him for her life. She buried the heart of her friend, as was garou custom, and crafted armour and bow from his scales and bones. Her friend would be with her, always, as companion in her hunt.

item_168.lead: The ring of life is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring grants players automatic teleportation to their bed or bed roll upon reaching 10% health. Once that happens, the ring becomes broken, requiring 1 Vault Core to repair. The recipe is unlocked through Death's Exchange for 800 soul fragments.

journal.text: Harold has a job for you and won’t let something as trivial as your expired mortality get in the way. This piece of enchanted jewellery is primed to go off when you’re about to land on Death’s list, whisking you away to safety before the scythe needs to be swung. There are many sorcerers that have studied these rings for years, going slowly mad as they try to uncover the secrets of immortality. If they could just learn the methods by which this ring operates, they could extend their lives indefinitely. Only one wizard ever actually learned this secret, but he forgot the method by which this ring works, for it teleports you at the moment of your death. As the ring does not stop the aging process, this unfortunate mage now spends his eternity in perpetual teleportation – hurled through the abyss, never to take form again.

item_169.desc: A magical ring that makes you sneakier.
item_169.lead: The ring of pursuit is a trinket, made on the jeweler's bench. Its special effect reduces animals’ awareness of your presence by 80%. For example, if the awareness radius of the deer is 50 metres, wearing the trinket will decrease the radius by 40 metres.

journal.text: Hunters have always needed an edge, and this ring is just that. It enhances a hunter's senses and quitens their movements. Their prey becomes less wary of them and more vulnerable to attach. The garou were particularly fond of these rings, and during the few years of peace between the humans of Bramblemead and the garou of Ghornfell, villagers could barter these trinkets for far more than they were worth to other villagers.

item_170.lead: The ring of recoil is a ring that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the ring deals percentage of damage received back to attackers. The damage dealt is equal to 50% of the damage taken, rounded up.

journal.text: Vengeance isn’t a dish best served cold, but one served quickly. Whilst taking years to enact the cruellest retaliation might work in the civilised world, in the wilds of Ashenfall a quick strike is far more valuable. This ring was first created by one of the Amalgamated, worn as both deterrence and for some small satisfaction when they were targeted by vigilante mobs. It didn’t prevent the bruises, or fix the broken bones, but their assailants attacks would end much more quickly when they discovered they weren’t as untouchable as they thought.

item_173.lead: The salve amulet is an amulet that can be crafted at a jeweler's bench. While equipped, the amulet increases damage against undead monsters by 17%. An effigy with a glowing ball at the Skekven Kara vault gives a stone dwarven tablet, which, after talking to Doric, grants a recipe for the salve amulet. Players will receive a salve crystal (required for creating the amulet) in return for this exchange. Loses 3 durability per hit on undead enemies, meaning it will break after ~833 hits.

journal.text: The name is a bit of a misnomer, since this amulet has very little to do with the Salve river. Instead its name refers to the crystal that traditionally sits at the heart. This crystal was first brought to the region by Saradominist priests, sometime in the Third Age. They had harvested it from a cave near the Salve river and found ways to cultivate it on Ashenfall’s soil, by utilising the natural magic infusing everything. Sanctified by faith and magic, this amulet was fatal to the undead, and the dragonkin Lacrussa was fascinated with the properties. She stole the recipe for its creation and hid it within her vault, long before the withering curse spread over Fellhollow. Instead she had delved too deeply in her own experiments and discovered something buried within the earth that would twist and reanimate the dead. This amulet allowed her to hold the forces back and keep them from overrunning her lab. That was until she met her end at Kuldra’s fangs.

journal.text: Priests of Saradomin would often wear cloaks like these. Simple affairs, designed to keep them safe from the breeze whilst also venerating the god of order. Both practical and fashionable. A good Saradominist always looks their best in any weather.

journal.text: The Shadow Knights, or Black Knights as they would come to be known, were mostly melee and ranged fighters. When magic was needed, they would enlist Alric's magi, but that secondment was always short. The melee knights were mostly posted in the grounds, but the ranged knights had a different role: they were stationed around the demon gate. Archmage Alric came to Lord Rasmodel with a sheet of paper. It was morning, when the Master of Dowdun was most impatient. Alric had been monitoring the Black Knights. He had suspected something for years now, but today he had proof. The sheet was from a ledger, and it had accounted for the number of magi casualties since Alric had become Archmage. There had been one hundred and seventeen deaths from one hundred and seventeen separate incidents. There was no single incident in which more than one mage had died. Alric was in a fury, tossing papers and spitting curses. It was proof that the Shadow Knights were deliberately negligent, that they saw the magi as disposable. Lord Rasmodel and let the mage rampage. The orders went out from Lord Rasmodel the next day. All Shadow Knights were to allow two magi to die with each incident.

journal.text: The Shadow Knights, or Black Knights as they would come to be known, were mostly melee and ranged fighters. When magic was needed, they would enlist Alric's magi, but that secondment was always short. The melee knights were mostly posted in the grounds, but the ranged knights had a different role: they were stationed around the demon gate. Lord Rasmodel's greatest challenge came from within. It did not carry a sword or crossbow. The Shadow Knight numbers were dropping. It was impossible to resign from the order -- that was written in the charter -- but more and more of the knights were falling into madness. If it were physical wounds, Lord Rasmodel could have done something about the epidemic. He could amputate the problem with a single swing of his sword. But his enemy was intangible. He decided to visit those on the precipice of madness. Most of them were unintelligible, but some talked of food not satisfying them anymore. Others called out to the Dreaming Stone like it was their mother, as if it would save them. In many cases, it sounds like the afflicted were arguing with themselves: two enemies unleashing an enmity. One of the mindless disquieted Lord Rasmodel more than the others. She was an afflicted soldier that he knew from long ago. She rambled in a voice that mimicked the droning of a bored aristocrat. Lord Rasmodel knew that voice well. He stumbled from the bedside of the soldier and took no other visitors that day.

journal.text: The Shadow Knights, or Black Knights, as they would come to be known, were mostly melee and ranged fighters. When magic was needed, they would enlist Alric's magi, but that secondment was always short. The melee knights were mostly posted in the grounds, but the ranged knights had a different role: they were stationed around the demon gate. Lord Rasmodel gave his Black Knights two sets of orders. The first they were free to discuss, and were encouraged to do so. They were there to protect the magi from the demons. Should one break from its bindings, it was to be put down. In an outbreak situation, the Shadow Knights had full jurisdiction and a freedom to kill with impunity. The second set of orders was not to be discussed, not even in the company of another. There were two salient instructions. Instruction 1: The Shadow Knights would allow for the 'Demon's Share'. Should a demon become unruly, one single mage fatality was encouraged before the demon was to be put down. It was like the culling of rabbits. The mage numbers needed to be managed. Instruction 2: Should the flow of demons be too much for the magi to control, the Shadow Knights were to collapse the infernal portal. This was the primary directive: the demons and magi were secondary.

journal.text: Not all magic is focused on the obliteration of one’s enemies; though many would argue that’s where the fun lies. No, magic can also improve the rest of one’s life in similarly impressive ways. This necklace, favoured by artisans, miners, lumberjacks and similar, is an example of such magic. The enchantment is simple, it enhances ones luck. When swinging at a rock, you have a higher chance of finding that weak seam. If cutting down a tree, the forces acting on your cuts make it easier to fell it. You are a little luckier in your endeavours and therefore get better results. In the Wizard’s Tower this has caused no end of arguments. Luck, isn’t a thing. It’s not a law of creation, nor a principle on which the measured universe runs. Cause has Effect. Doing one action creates an outcome, a different action another. Luck, whilst popular with the layperson, isn’t something that can be measured or refined, it’s simply coincidence, nothing more. Yet, this necklance proves that it must be a thing. Even though it can’t be. Therefore this little trinket has been the source of some of the longest, loudest and most violent debates for decades.

journal.text: Not all druids follow the notion that one must live a life of peaceful coexistence. After all, the animal kingdom is full of conflict and conquest, predator and prey, as well as battles for dominance. Some druids feel, therefore, that to truly emulate nature one must do so fully, including tooth and claw. The problem is that druids are by nature generally on the squishier side and so they needed armour that would protect their vital areas better than their normal robes. Soon, many druids began wearing these robes made from the bark of Ashenfall trees. The first incarnations were deeply unwieldy, taking on an ungainly and unfashionable cylindrical shape - little more than tree trunks with holes for the arms and legs. They were effective insomuch that attacks rarely got through, but they made it somewhat difficult to retaliate. Later the wizard Lavernius realises that with a few tweaks, the addition of some elegant fine cloth, one could fashion the splitbark armour into a far more glamorous form. She took to decorating her robes with glittering gemstones and silver filigree, making her stand out from the crowd. An excellent distraction in magical duels, but a terrible spotlight for local thieves.

The problem is that druids are by nature generally on the squishier side and so they needed armour that would protect their vital areas better than their normal robes. After having her glittering armour stolen, Lavernius decided that she was tired of being "Miss Nice Wizard" and crafted a versino of the armour that would blend worryingly well into the local scenery. She crept up on her robbers as they spent an evening trying to prize gemstones from what remained of her helmet, and she unleashed her terrible revenge. Thousands of chinchompas, each of them suffering from a powerful confusion, were turned upon the miscreants. The resulting explosion was so bright that it turned night into day for a moment, and the flames spread with worrying rapacity. Later bandits soon agreed that Lavernius was to be given a very wide berth.

journal.text: It is said these swamps are haunted. Those who wander it at night, tell stories of whispering that bubbles up from the fetid water. There is a coldness to these swamps, that is more than just temperature. It reaches beneath the warmest clothing and presses itself into bone and blood. Heartbeats slow and bravery breaks beneath its touch. The trees here are old and spiteful, their roots wrapped around the bones of adventurers, villagers, and warriors alike. They care not for goblin, human, or garou, they will strangle the remains of any within their reach. Occasionally tiny stones will bubble from the surface, black as midnight and cold as the darkest winter night. A villager once tried to craft jewelry from these stones, thinking them beautiful. It took twelve village guard to put an end to her murder spree. This cape is woven from the fibres of swamp plants, and shields its wearer from the swamp’s whispers. Or so the old wives tales claim.

journal.text: Sir Percival Lateef only had a short moment of wonder, before the horror struck. The beach he had arrived on was surrounded by cliffs, meaning his only options were to climb or to swim, and since he was wearing the heavy armour of the White Knights, he decided that sinking wasn’t an option. It took him many hours and several near falls, but he eventually made his way up and down the cliffside, only to encounter a region filled with the ravenous undead. As a White Knight he trained to fight such evils and he fended them off as best he could, yet there were too many for him to face alone. He was forced to retreat, to a shrine, atop a rocky island, displaying the symbol of Saradomin, and there he prayed.

journal.text: Trapped by a shrine that stood atop a rocky island, surrounded by the hungry dead, Sir Lateef prayed to Saradomin with all his strength. He begged for salvation, for a miracle that might free him, but silence was his only answer. He barricaded himself atop the monument, the dead scrabbling at his defences, their unholy growling keeping him from even a moment’s sleep. As time drew on, and hunger and thirst took him, he turned to the symbol of Saradomin in defeated rage. Where was his god? Why was he abandoned? Had he not spent his life in service of the lord of light? Enraged, he took his sword and cleaved Saradomin’s symbol from its plinth, causing it to crash to the floor. Filled with guilt, he hid the fallen piece from his sight. His last act was one of blasphemy, but perhaps an act justly performed.

journal.text: The Wild Knights were known for their ability to scout the wild areas of Ashenfall. They could walk where no one else dared to tread, and they were masters of the hunt — putting even the garou to shame. Their archers wore sturdy leathers, using carefully laid folds to shield them against harm. They would break easily, but the archers made it part of their ritual to maintain them regularly. Each day, they would wake and tend to the leather, making their armour seem brand new with each morning. Archers of the Wild Knights were quick, silent and deadly. They could stalk their prey, silent and slowly, sometimes taking days between kills as they followed their quarry around the lands. They would hunt monsters and people with equal focus, as dictated by the order’s commands. To harm the wilds was to make yourself a target for the Wild Knights. To sully the green lands of Guthix, an unforgivable crime. Yet, there were always those who would risk their ire, wannabe despots and greedy fools yearning to plunder the realm. They all met the fate they deserved, in the end.

journal.text: These blue robes are the signature clothing worn by every respectable mage. Apprentices look forward to the day they first wear these, as it shows they have graduated to full wizard status. The Wizard's Tower, in particular, uses these robes as a uniform, signifying their magical power and fealty to the god of order, Saradomin. On Ashenfall, it was rare for those wearing these robes to be seen outside the Wizard's Guild. The structure on the hillside was home to strange practices and even stranger experiments. Powerful spells were studied and unleashed across an already magically problematic countryside. The White Knights, often summoned to address the perils that the Wizard's Guild inadvertently unleashed, were a frequent presence. Their duties ranged from quelling peculiar weather phenomena to managing the "accidental" summoning of demons. To maintain control, a contingent of knights established a permanent residence within the guild, their vigilant eyes ever watchful.

journal.text: Zamorak never came to Dowdun Reach. Its gates were never graced by the mahjarrat. No general came, or ambassador from the mainland. Even the ZMI failed to send an offshoot to the keep. How was that possible? Chaos taught them that, by simple laws of averages, a high-ranking Zamorakian should have stumbled onto their shores. Ashenfall and Dowdun Reach was too much of an opportunity. Greed must have led a Zamorakian highborn here. The silence was deafening. Everyone who lived or worked in the keep knew what this meant: Zamorak had barred his inner circle from visiting Ashenfall, likely at pain of death. How else could Dowdun Reach have been left alone for so long? But why? Why did Zamorak keep Ashenfall at arm's length? The answers differed, depending on the zeal of the follower. Zamorak feared something on Ashenfall. Zamorak knew that something made it worthless. Zamorak was already here, just without Dowdun's knowing. Zamorak is in all of us. Remarkably, that mystery only strengthened the beliefs of Dowdun's Zamorakians. By being so contemptible to Zamorak, they were utterly important. They were main characters in Zamorak's performance. It suggests another reason why Zamorak might have left Ashenfall alone. Perhaps he wanted to show that nothing - not even his disdain - would soften his people's infatuation.

item_219.lead: Agility flags are a reward for completing the Thunder Assault Agility course at silver or gold tier and can be built by the player. To build it, players must have at least 1 oak log, 1 padded cloth, and 1 warped feather.

item_223.lead: The armour bench is a crafting station that allows the creation of head armour, body armour, leg armour (all styles: melee, magic, ranged), cape slot equipment (capes + other). This replaces, in part, the functionality of the smithing anvil, crafting table, and the jeweler's bench.

item_224.lead: An armour mannequin is a buildable object at level 40 Artisan, which players can mount up to five pieces of armour. Players can quickly swap armours at mannequins and can even store some capes on them (Pioneer's cape the dragonbane cape and Fellhollow cape). If a certain piece of equipment is already on a mannequin, players can add another piece of the same type. For example, if the reinforced helmet is on the mannequin, players can also add a Dragonkin mage hood. This results in only the latter being shown.

item_225.lead: The ash chest is a small storage container for up to 32 item slots. Players can unlock the small chest by receiving ash logs in their inventory for the first time and unlocking the skill perk Creature Comforts. Players can also name their chest, up to 16 characters long. To craft or process an item without having the required items in their inventory, players must have the required items in their chest and check the "Linked" checkbox in the chest interface. This will allow players to craft up to a 12-metre radius away from the chest.

item_226.lead: The ash farming plot can be used to grow plants with seeds through the Farming skill. Ash farming plots must be placed on the ground without a roof overhead. In addition, ash farming plots have three stages of weeds that players must dig after setting an ash farming plot on the ground.

item_227.lead: The bed is a buildable piece of furniture used to rest and set the player's respawn point in the world. If used at night, players will skip to daytime and regain their full rest meter; if used during the day, players will lie in place and slowly regain their rest meter over time. The bed requires 8 ash planks and 4 rough cloth to craft, and must be under a roof and enclosed with three walls to be used.

item_228.lead: The bed roll is a buildable piece of furniture used to rest and set the player's respawn point in the world. If used at night, players will skip to daytime and regain their full rest meter; if used during the day, players will lie in place and slowly regain their rest meter over time. The bed roll requires 3 ash logs and 3 coarse animal fur to craft, and must be under a roof and enclosed with three walls to be used.

item_229.lead: The blacksmith's bench is a buildable facility where players can only create weapons that are higher tiered than stone equipment. The blacksmith's bench replaced the smithing anvil in the game, and is unlocked upon obtaining a bronze bar in the player's inventory.

It requires fuel pellets to operate, which can be obtained by combining charcoal, adhesive, and coarse animal fur at a blacksmith's bench. Its operation can be greatly sped up by casting Superheat on it, and it must not have a roof above it to function.
