journal.text: The wizard Mallory was never as good as he had hoped to be. He was proficient in spellcasting and his rote memory was excellent, but the power of his spells always fell a little short. His advancement through the ranks was due more to being around long enough than anything else, and he never quite earned the respect of his peers. That was until the day he created the focus. Mallory had always been good at making things. He enjoyed the simpler magic of crafting, and he found you could weave small threads of magic into the construction of something, breathing just a little bit more life and wonder into it than before. True craftsmanship, he believed, carried a little bit of the creator’s soul in it. The focus proved this theory and elevated it further. By creating a focus and subconsciously imbuing it with a bit of his essence, it facilitated a smoother, more fluid, channel of magic through the body. This resulted in spells of greater potency. Tragically, after sharing his knowledge with the other wizards, he was murdered by his mentor, who claimed the knowledge as his own. Karma is a stern judge, however, and the offending wizard later found himself being swallowed whole and digested by a dragon. Just punishment, I’m sure Mallory would agree.

journal.text: The Moon Garou don't recognise the term 'monk'. It's very much a Saradominist or Zamorakian term (strange how the customs of the two gods are so similar, don't you think?). The Moon Garou are more shamanistic, and do not understand or care for things like 'denying yourself worldly pleasures'. It is their belief that when there are so few fruits and treasures in the desert, why would someone possibly deny themselves a moment of enjoyment? Which raises the question of why the Moon Garou call these fish 'monkfish' at all. Well, the answer is a little on the boring, perhaps even obvious side. The River Goddess, who many Moon Garou worship, came to Ashenfall from mainland Gielinor, where the monkfish are more prevalent. So she pointed at the fish, said its name, and Bob's your monkfish.

item_723.desc: Tasty monkfish meat, pierced on a skewer for convenient eating.

They are made with monkfish fillets and seared cactus steak in a stone range or a cooking range, however a player must interact with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

journal.text: Monkfish skewers are the friend of any travelling Moon Garou. Compact and easy to carry, a couple of dozen can be taken on any scouting or hunting party. They also double-up as weapons, should a garou find themselves ambushed during a hearty meal. It's not uncommon to see a half-dead kalphite staggering about in the desert with rows of monkfish skewers puncturing their carapace. They look a little like a buffet dish.

journal.text: A taste of autumn reduced to slurry and warmed over the fire. In Fellhollow, pumpkin soup was a popular dish when the temperature started to drop. Locals would gather together and share enormous cauldrons full of soup, as a way to build bonds with their community. It is said that once the villagers created an enormous cauldron, so that Imaru and Xikotal could join in the tradition, though for the great dragons it was barely an appetiser.

journal.text: On the sea voyage to Ashenfall, Zanik went through a period of shouting 'lobster!' at the end of perfectly normal conversations with her shipmates. She claimed it was a joke that young dorgeshuun would play on each other, but it led to her being roundly ignored by Vannaka and Dionysius for several days. It's also a roasted food - one that makes you feel more refreshed and less thirsty after eating it. If you are to attempt to cook one, it is recommended that you... LOBSTER!

item_763.lead: Roast pumpkin is a consumable food item that provides 20 health and 25 sustenance, as well as the perk Soul Food, which restores 8 health every 5 seconds for 150 seconds. It can be cooked from pumpkin at either a campfire or a grill, and is used in dubious meat pie, pumpkin soup, pumpkin spice infusion, glazed pumpkin sandwich, and Umbral kebab.

journal.text: Whilst some prefer to hollow out a pumpkin, carving features into it that should scare away the creatures of the night, more practical people eat them. A roasted pumpkin is a hearty affair, full of texture and a mellow taste that goes especially well in desserts.

item_764.desc: Made by combining fried sardine and dried redberry. Grants the Warding Fish perk.
item_764.lead: Sauteed sardines are a consumable food item that provides 70 health and 25 sustenance, as well as granting the perk Sea Life, which restores 3 health every second for 600 seconds. They are made with fried sardine and dried redberries in a stone range or a cooking range; however, a player must interact with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

journal.text: A fried sardine, also known as a charred pilchard or 'pilcharred', is the go-to snack for a fisherman's pocket. If you see a stoic fisherman who talks very little, it's likely because they've got a mouthful of fried sardine and don't want to reveal the bones between their teeth. Fried sardines were also the subject of a failed business venture by a dwarf called Drorkar. He tried to manufacture 'tins' that would contain these sardines, with smithed 'rings' to open their tiny metal coffins. It was roundly rejected and cost the dwarf a great deal.

item_765.desc: A simple meal but one that will hold back the hunger.
item_765.lead: Sauteed shrimp is a consumable food item that provides 20 health and 10 sustenance. It is made by cooking raw shrimp on either a campfire or a grill, and is used in shrimp omelette and weak Focused Fishing potion.

journal.text: In a burst of freakish coincidence, the shrimp is both the easiest sea creature to catch, and the easiest to cook. As a result, some folk from seafaring towns have been known to call shrimp 'eggs of the sea'. Both are considered over-easy. If you burned rather than sauteed a shrimp, congratulations! In some towns, a burnt shrimp is considered a rarity, such is the negligence required to make one.

item_766.lead: Seared anchovies are a consumable food item that provide 30 health and 15 sustenance. They are made by cooking raw anchovies on either a campfire or a grill, and are used in berry drizzle pan-seared.

journal.text: Not be confused with Seered Anchovies: a delicacy from Umbral Sands where the anchovies are lightly toasted on clairvoyants. The naturally salty taste of an anchovy has been ascribed to salt flats on the ocean floor, where anchovies feed on the underwater flora. In an attempt to deepen the anchovy flavour, fishermen have been known to sprinkle pepper, marrentil and pineapple on those same salt flats.

item_767.desc: You'd be surprised at how tasty an eight-ounce cactus, medium-rare can be.
item_767.lead: Cactus steak is a Power Level 5 consumable food item that provides 20 health and 20 sustenance when eaten. It can be cooked from cactus steak at either a campfire or grill. It requires Cooking level 50 to cook and 75 to not burn, otherwise creating Burnt Cactus Steak.

journal.text: Look, not everyone gets to tuck into a redberry pie every night. Sometimes you have to make do, using the resources you have to hand. A cactus steak is very much 'making do': it's prickly to prepare, as you might expect, and tough to eat. It's the kind of meal that makes a garou cub eyeroll and ask whether something other than cactus steak will be on the menu tomorrow. It doesn't matter that it's what nutritionists call a 'superfood', offering some alphabetical variety of vitamins. It's just not particularly exciting or flavoursome, and you might find your cubs making excuses to be elsewhere at dinnertime.

item_768.desc: Made by combining fried egg and sauté shrimp. Grants the Sea Legs perk.
item_768.lead: Shrimp omelette is a consumable food item that provides 50 health and 15 sustenance as well as the perk Sea Legs, which makes you immune to the slowing effects of water for 600 seconds. It is made with fried egg and sauteed shrimp in a stone range or a cooking range, however a player must interact with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

journal.text: It was inevitable that shrimp, known as the 'eggs of the sea' for being over-easy to catch, would get combined with actual eggs to form a meal. Shrimp Omelette is the go-to feast for a shipman, often whipped up by the ship's cook and delivered en masse to the crew. If you're assigned to a long-haul crew, it's best to get a taste for the 'Shrompy' (as it's often shortened). Shrompy is also common among Wizards' Guild students who only have space in their dorms for a frying pan and some fire runes.

item_769.desc: A dusty sack that rattles when you shake it.
item_769.lead: Skeleton packs are a drop from skeletons.

journal.text: A foul-smelling sack, with threads frayed by the cruelty of time. Contains whatever strange possessions were being hoarded after death.

item_770.desc: There seems to be something solid in the ash pile.
item_770.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_770.lead: Small ash piles are a drop from hellrat and hellhound.

item_771.desc: Nothing beats hunger like a herring. Grants the Warding Fish perk.
item_771.lead: Smoked herring is a consumable food item that provides 50 health and 20 sustenance. It is made by cooking raw herring on either a campfire or a grill, and is used in berry drizzle pan-seared.

journal.text: Smoked herring is not, as the idiom will claim, 'red'. It is more of an orange, coppery colour. That means the term 'red herring' is something of a red herring. Which tracks. The process of smoking a herring has changed over the years. In the Second Age, a herring would be smoked in the village elder's pipe, in the hope that some of the elder's wisdom would transfer to the fish. In the Third Age, entrepreneurial Zamorakians would line their demon portals with herring in the hope of an infernal aftertaste. Nowadays, people use a cooking pot.

item_772.desc: An unusual meal, but a good one. Grants the Warding Fish perk.
item_772.lead: Smoked infernal eel is a consumable food item that provides 100 health and 30 sustenance. It is made by cooking raw infernal eel on either a campfire or a grill, and is used in stir-fry.

journal.text: One of the most challenging dishes to prepare on Ashenfall is the smoked infernal eel. The whole process is an olfactory gauntlet. You are bombarded with such a succession of smells, some wonderful, some horrifying, that it can feel like sprinting through the back alleys of Varrock. Some chefs from the Cook's Guild have compared it to 'seeing one's life flash before their eyes'. Except with noses. Complete the gauntlet, however, and the bounty is worth it. Many people call smoked infernal eel a 'delicacy' but the term doesn't really suit. Delicacy is derived from 'delicate', after all. The taste is more like a salt-chinchompa exploding under your tongue.

item_774.lead: Squeaking sausage is a consumable food item that provides +0.5 Resist Shocked Buildup, 80 health, and 80 sustenance as well as the perk Grounded, which grants resistance to shock effects for 300 seconds. It is made with dried dwellberries, fried onions, and rat roast in a cooking range.

item_775.desc: Consuming a stamina potion will prevent all loss of stamina for a short duration, however you'll need a moment to recover before you have another as such unbridled energy is taxing on the body.
item_775.lead: Stamina potion grants the perk Stamina Potion, preventing stamina drain from all actions for 20 seconds. Upon using the potion, the player must wait roughly 75 seconds (1 minute and 15 seconds) starting from consumption to use another potion. This, effectively, means players must wait 55 seconds after the potion effect ends to use another dose if players want to multi-dose. ==Recipe==

journal.text: The frustrating thing about agility courses is that you can't keep doing them forever. Agility's final boss is lactic acid, and it likes to stick spears into your muscles and joints. Well, the humble stamina potion is +1 against lactic acid. If you're planning on physical activity and want to flick the bird to exhaustion, then we would recommend making one or two.

item_776.desc: A delicious steak. The perfect campfire meal.
item_776.lead: Steak a consumable food item that provide 20 sustenance and 30 health when eaten. They can be cooked at either a campfire or grill.

item_777.desc: A marvelous way, to start your day.
item_777.lead: Steak 'n' eggs is a consumable food item that provides 40 health and 50 sustenance. It is made with fried egg and steak in a stone range or a cooking range, however a player must interact with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

item_778.desc: A delectable treat made with flank steak, fried onions and grilled mushrooms.
item_778.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_778.lead: Steak sandwich is a consumable food item that provides +0.5 Resist Shocked Buildup, 90 health and 80 sustenance as well as the perks Coagulated, Grounded, and Fungal Fortitude, which reduces Bleed buildup, reduces the amount of Shock damage taken, and reduces Poison buildup by 33% for 600 seconds. It is made with flank steak, fried onions, grilled mushrooms, and bread in a cooking range after finding the recipe in The Cathedral in Dowdun Reach.

journal.text: Steak, if you ask me, is infinitely diminished by putting it between two slices of bread. Steak should stand proud on its own, garnished with salt and barely introduced to a flame. As a journal-writer I can't stop you. My powers are limited to shaming you from the dark recesses of your interfaces.

item_779.desc: A long, tough meal. Don't eat it in one swallow.
item_779.lead: Steamed beltfish is a consumable food item that provides 100 health and 30 sustenance. It is made by cooking raw beltfish on either a campfire or a grill, and is used in beltfish broth and swabbie pie.

journal.text: The custom with a steamed beltfish is to eat it all in one, like a sword-eater swallowing their blade whole. The Moon Garou chomp it down like they were raised by pythons. The human gullet isn't quite built for this method of eating, so be careful if you're invited over for a Moon Garou celebration. Aim for the smaller ones at the banquet table. Chew subtly.

item_780.desc: Made by combining dried giant krill, dried redberry and smoked infernal eel.
item_780.lead: Stir-fry is a consumable food item that provides 150 health and 70 sustenance as well as the perks Sea Legs and Sea Life, which makes players immune to the slowing effects of water and restores 3 health every second for 600 seconds. It is made with dried giant krill, dried dwellberries, and smoked infernal eel in a cooking range.

journal.text: Imagine if we named all our meals after the processes that make it. Ooh, I'm going to make a pot of boil-strain-pour. I might follow it up with a batch of roll-cut-bakes. It's all a bit odd, if you ask me. The Ashenfall stir-fry is something of a curio when compared to the mainland's. To make a mainland version, you would have to swap the krill for seaweed and the infernal eel for lava eel. Whisper it, though: I think the Ashenfall version is better. And it goes particularly well with some grow-chop-fries.

item_781.lead: Strong sweet tea is a consumable drink item that provides 10 hydration and 20 rest as well as the perk Sugar Rush, which reduces rest drain by 25% for 300 seconds. It is made with ground tea leaves, 3 clean water, and maple syrup in a cooking range.

item_782.lead: Strong tea is a consumable drink item that provides 10 hydration and 20 rest. It is made with ground tea leaves and 3 clean water in a cooking range.

item_783.desc: Made by combining dried giant krill, fried cabbage and a braised catfish.
item_783.lead: Stuffed catfish is a consumable food item that provides 200 health and 80 sustenance. It is made with dried giant krill, fried cabbage, and braised catfish in a cooking range.

journal.text: Perhaps it's a good thing that fish have no idea what their future holds. We can only imagine their reactions. "Sorry, chap, you're going to have your armour removed, your innards replaced with cabbage, and krill pushed into your orifices." Would it soften the blow if they knew how tasty they became? A stuffed catfish is elevated by the brassic flavours, achieving culinary peaks that are unrivalled on Ashenfall. We like to think that the knowledge would soften the blow.

item_784.desc: Even when cooked it still smells a great deal.
item_784.lead: Sun baked sole is a consumable food item that provides 130 health and 30 sustenance. It is made by cooking raw desert sole on either a campfire or a grill, and is used in swabbie pie.

journal.text: Most Moon Garou would consider an adventurer's version of dune-smoking to be a pale imitation of the true process. 'Real' dune-smoking involves burying a raw desert sole deep within a dune, preferably a couple of metres down. Inside the dune, it alternately cooks and cools with the Scorch and cold nights. The sand helps to delay the rotting process, but - I am slightly debatably told by Moon Garou chefs - that a little bit of rotting never hurt anyone.

item_785.desc: PERK: Antifire NEGATES and grants RESISTANCE to FIRE effects
item_785.lead: Super Antifire potion grants the perk Antifire, which removes Burning stacks and grants 33% resistance from Burning buildup for 600 seconds (10 minutes). It is made by using an Antifire potion in an imbuing barrel.

journal.text: This potion was created by a Moon Garou chef with ambitious far greater than their common sense. They yearned to create the greatest grilled steak ever made and required rather more fire than their kitchen was equipped to handle. The resulting conflagration was so impressive, that it inspired a local alchemist to create this magnificent countermeasure.

item_786.desc: PERK: Antipoison II NEGATES and grants RESISTENCE to POISON effects
item_786.lead: Super Antipoison potion grants the perk Antipoison II, which negates and grants resistance to Poison for 10 minutes (600 seconds).

journal.text: Once the desert was full of snakes, until they were banished below the sands by an angry goddess. Only rarely do they manage to break through the surface of the dunes to bite someone, and their venom has been concentrated so heavily by their solitude, that it’s lethal to anyone that suffers it. Fortunately, the shamans were able to create this antipoison, stronger and more powerful than previous tiers. It has saved many lives."

item_787.desc: PERK: Focused Agility II Grants a 30% XP BOOST for the Agility Skill
item_787.lead: Super Focused Agility potion grants the perk Focused Agility II, which provides a 10-minute (600-second) +30% XP boost for the Agility skill. It is made by using a Focused Agility potion in an imbuing barrel.

journal.text: This potion gives you lumber tunnel vision, where the tunnel is made of tasteful wood rather than bricks. All there is - aside from the tunnel - is you and the tree, mano et arboro. One of the greatest, most heated rivalries of all time.

item_788.desc: PERK: Focused Artisan II Grants a 30% XP BOOST for the ARTISAN Skill
item_788.lead: Super Focused Artisan potion grants the perk Focused Artisan II, which increased the experience gained through the Artisan skill by 30% for 10 minutes (600 seconds).

journal.text: Fermented with wild anima, this potion is a concentrated and more powerful version of its predecessor. The effects last longer and yet the power of the potion loses none of its efficiency. Be warned, after drinking this potion, you may find yourself dreaming of assembling furniture, painting little clay decorations, and a billion other little crafty things that you would never have dreamed of before. Just beware not to dream of the forbidden macramé, for in its strange knots do dark secrets dwell.

item_789.desc: PERK: Focused Attack II Grants a 30% XP BOOST for the ATTACK Skill
item_789.lead: Super Focused Attack potion grants the perk Focused Attack II, which provides a 10-minute (600-second) +30% XP boost for the Attack skill. It is made by using a Focused Attack potion in an imbuing barrel.

journal.text: Have you ever wondered what it would be like to know nothing but bloodlust? To know nothing but the call for battle and the need to slaughter? Well, with this potion, you can! Condensed and fermented alongside wild anima, this potion will flood your system with so much adrenaline and aggression, that you’ll be looking to cause destruction on a catastrophic scale.

item_790.desc: PERK: Focused Construction II Grants a 30% XP BOOST for the CONTRSTUCTION Skill
item_790.lead: Super Focused Construction potion grants the perk Focused Construction II, which provides a 10-minute (600-second) +30% XP boost for the Construction skill. It is made by using a Focused Construction potion in an imbuing barrel.

journal.text: Ah, to be a zen-like architect, focused on nothing but crenulations and scaffolding. Such thoughts were nought but dreams before this potion, yet now you have a chance to soar to new heights of… err… masonry? It’s hard to write about a potion that enhances your desire to build things. To wax lyrical about a liquid that grants greater XP when you craft new decorations and bigger stairs. Yet, here we are.

item_791.desc: PERK: Focused Cooking II Grants a 30% XP BOOST for the COOKING Skill
item_791.lead: Super Focused Cooking potion grants the perk Focused Cooking II, which provides a 10-minute (600-second) +30% XP boost for the Cooking skill. It is made by using a Focused Cooking potion in an imbuing barrel.

journal.text: This potion imbues you with the desire to bake. Cakes, pies, biscuits, battas, all things culinary become your obsession. While under its effects, you will grow to understand more about nutrition and flavour profiles. You will transcend the limits of your taste buds into realms of deliciousness that only Brassica Prime can comprehend. Use this potion wisely.

item_792.desc: PERK: Focused Farming II Grants a 30% XP BOOST for the FARMING Skill
item_792.lead: Super Focused Farming potion grants the perk Focused Farming II, which provides a 10-minute (600-second) +30% XP boost for the Farming skill. It is made by using a Focused Farming potion in an imbuing barrel.

journal.text: It's possible to imagine a super-focused angler or lumberjack, but a super-focused farmer? How much more can they get from a farming patch? A super-focused farmer is a disconcerting beast. They will sit at the corner of a farming patch, staring intensely at a seed, willing it to grow. They will do this for hours, even days, depending on the dosage. I'm not sure if the plant feels self-conscious or a little guilty, but it works: the plant does actually grow at a faster rate.

item_793.desc: PERK: Focused Fishing II Grants a 30% XP BOOST for the FISHING Skill
item_793.lead: Super Focused Fishing potion grants the perk Focused Fishing II, which provides a 10-minute (600-second) +30% XP boost for the Fishing skill. It is made by using a Focused Fishing potion in an imbuing barrel.

journal.text: If you want evidence of the strength of a super focused fishing potion, then look no further than Granny Potterington, who got mixed up and accidentally poured some into her pond. She came back the next day to find that one single fish had caught and eaten all the other fish in the pond. It had a confused look on its face and blood across its mouth and fins. Potent stuff.

item_794.desc: PERK: Focused Mining II Grants a 30% XP BOOST for the MINING Skill
item_794.lead: Super Focused Mining potion grants the perk Focused Mining II, which provides a 10-minute (600-second) +30% XP boost for the Mining skill. It is made by using a Focused Mining potion in an imbuing barrel.

item_795.desc: PERK: Focused Runecrafting II Grants a 30% XP BOOST for the RUNECRAFING Skill
item_795.lead: Super Focused Runecrafting potion grants the perk Focused Runecrafting II, which provides a 10-minute (600-second) +30% XP boost for the Runecrafting skill. It is made by using a Focused Runecrafting potion in an imbuing barrel.

journal.text: I once met a magician and runecrafter who managed to heighten her senses through super focused runecrafting potions. Her party trick was to apply a blindfold and be handed several runes. She could tell you the exact runes by licking, sniffing and fondling the stones. I'm not entirely sure whether this was an ability gained from the potion, or if she was just oddly aware of the properties of runes. A bit of a downside was that, if you made her a meal, drink or even passed close to her, she would say "ooh, that tastes a bit of air runes" or "you smell like a law rune". It's hard to know what to do with that information.

item_796.desc: PERK: Focused Woodcutting II Grants a 30% XP BOOST for the WOODCUTTING Skill
item_796.lead: Super Focused Woodcutting potion grants the perk Focused Woodcutting II, which provides a 10-minute (600-second) +30% XP boost for the Woodcutting skill. It is made by using a Focused Woodcutting potion in an imbuing barrel.

journal.text: This potion gives you lumber tunnel vision, where the tunnel is made of tasteful wood rather than bricks. All there is - aside from the tunnel - is you and the tree, mano et arboro. One of the greatest, most heated rivalries of all time.

item_797.desc: PERK: Lumberjack II REDUCES the STAMINA cost of WOODCUTTING by 66%
item_797.lead: Super Lumberjack potion grants the perk Lumberjack II, which reduces the stamina cost of woodcutting by 66% for 10 minutes (600 seconds).

journal.text: Pour a lumberjack potion down your gullet, and you will feel like not tree could stop you. You will believe that you can move faster than a magic carpet, leap over trees with a single bound. You will believe that you can chop a forest with a single swing of your logging axe. Well, we're here to tell you that there is a reasonably large delta between what you believe you can do and what you can actually do. So prepare to be a little disappointed when you sober up.

item_798.desc: PERK: Quarrymaster II REDUCES the STAMINA cost of MINING by 66%
item_798.lead: Super Quarrymaster potion grants the perk Quarrymaster II, which reduces the stamina cost of mining by 66% for 10 minutes (600 seconds).

journal.text: A super quarrymaster potion will give you supernatural stamina when it comes to mining rocks, but you should be careful. Potions have the annoying habit of wearing off, and it's only then that you realise you've got killer cramp, pins and needles, or miner's cough. There's no comedown quite like a quarrymaster comedown.

item_799.desc: A pie reserved for the less prestigious members of a ship's crew.
item_799.lead: Swabbie pie is a consumable food item that provide 220 health and 80 sustenance. It is made with sun baked sole, steamed beltfish, bread, and baked potato in a cooking range.

item_800.desc: A marvelous amalgamation of sweet and savoury.
item_800.lead: Sweet veg ball is a consumable food item that provides 70 health 65 sustenance as well as the perk Knowledgable Nourishment, which increases the player's experience gain in all skills by 10% for 300 seconds. It is made with fried cabbage, baked potato, and dried redberries in a stone range or a cooking range. It is learned by unlocking Amateur Culinaromancer at level 16 Cooking, and requires interacting with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

journal.text: Popular among gnomes, this sticky ball of fruits and vegetables is a combination of savoury and sweet that almost feels like it shouldn’t work. Yet it does. There is a crispness to the outer shell, savoury and salty, which gives way to a delicious fruity sweetness beneath. Gnomish ambassadors would create large numbers of these sweet treats, piled high on silver platters, to delight visiting dignitaries at lavish receptions. Diplomats would often joke about being spoiled by such treats. Which is ironic really, as these spoil very quickly, so enjoy them now while you can.

item_801.desc: A book filled with knowledge on how to move more efficiently. Awards a small amount of Agility XP.
item_801.lead: Tome of Agility - Vol 1 is a skill tome that can be occasionally obtained through normal gameplay. When read, the tome gives 100 Agility experience. == Item sources == [Insert sources here]

item_802.desc: A book filled with knowledge on how to move more efficiently. Awards a decent amount of Agility XP.
item_802.lead: Tome of Agility - Vol 2 is a skill tome that can be found occasionally through gameplay. When read, the tome gives 400 Agility experience. == Item sources == [Insert sources here]

item_803.lead: Tome of Attack - Vol 1 is a skill tome that can be received occasionally from chests. When read, the tome gives 100 Attack experience.

item_804.desc: A book filled with knowledge on the use of melee weapons. Awards a decent amount of Attack XP.
item_804.lead: Tome of Attack - Vol 2 is a skill tome found in chests within Fellhollow. When read, the tome gives 400 Attack experience.

item_805.lead: Tome of Construction - Vol 1 is a skill tome that can be received occasionally from chests. When read, the tome gives 100 Construction experience.

item_806.lead: Tome of Construction - Vol 2 is a skill tome found in chests within Fellhollow. When read, the tome gives 400 Construction experience.

item_807.lead: Tome of Cooking - Vol 1 is a skill tome that is one of four rewards given after completing the Restless Ghosts quest. It can also be received occasionally from chests. When read, the tome gives 100 Cooking experience.

item_808.lead: Tome of Cooking - Vol 2 is a skill tome found in chests within Fellhollow. When read, the tome gives 400 Cooking experience.

item_809.lead: The Tome of Farming - Vol 1 is a tier 1 tome that rewards the player 100 Farming experience.

item_810.desc: A book filled with knowledge about how to apply dirt and water to seeds. Awards a decent amount of Farming XP.
item_810.lead: The Tome of Farming - Vol 2 is a tier 2 tome that rewards the player 400 Farming experience.

item_811.desc: A book filled with knowledge about how to efficiently tire out fish. Awards a small amount of Fishing XP.
item_811.lead: Tome of Fishing - Vol 1 is a skill tome that rewards the player 100 Fishing experience. Players can receive this tome through completing the quest, Shrimp Catcher.

item_812.desc: A book filled with knowledge about how to efficiently tire out fish. Awards a decent amount of Fishing XP.
item_812.lead: Tome of Fishing - Vol 2 is a skill tome that rewards the player 400 Fishing experience.

item_813.lead: Tome of Magic - Vol 1 is a skill tome that can be received occasionally from chests. When read, the tome gives 100 Magic experience.

item_814.desc: A book filled with knowledge on how to wield deadlier spells. Awards a decent amount of Magic XP.
item_814.lead: Tome of Magic - Vol 2 is a skill tome found in chests within Fellhollow. When read, the tome gives 400 Magic experience.

item_815.desc: A book filled with knowledge on the intricacies of archery. Awards a small amount of Ranged XP.
item_815.lead: Tome of Ranged - Vol 1 is a skill tome that can be received occasionally from chests. When read, the tome gives 100 Ranged experience.

item_816.desc: A book filled with knowledge on the intricacies of archery. Awards a decent amount of Ranged XP.
item_816.lead: Tome of Ranged - Vol 2 is a skill tome found in chests within Fellhollow. When read, the tome gives 400 Ranged experience.

item_817.desc: A book filled with knowledge on how to bind anima within rune essence. Awards a small amount of Runecrafting XP.
item_817.lead: Tome of Runecrafting - Vol 1 is a skill tome that is the reward given after completing the First Steps quest. It can also be received occasionally from chests. When read, the tome gives 100 Runecrafting experience.

item_818.desc: A book filled with knowledge on how to bind anima within rune essence. Awards a decent amount of Runecrafting XP.
item_818.lead: Tome of Runecrafting - Vol 2 is a skill tome found in chests within Fellhollow. When read, the tome gives 400 Runecrafting experience.

item_819.desc: A book filled with knowledge on how to craft tools and equipment. Awards a small amount of Artisan XP.
item_819.lead: Tome of the Artisan - Vol 1 is a skill tome that is one of four rewards given after completing the Restless Ghosts quest. It can also be received occasionally from chests. When read, the tome gives 100 Artisan experience.

item_820.desc: A book filled with knowledge on how to craft tools and equipment. Awards a decent amount of Artisan XP.
item_820.lead: Tome of the Artisan - Vol 2 is a skill tome found in chests within Fellhollow. When read, the tome gives 400 Artisan experience.

item_821.desc: A powerful tome containing ancient techniques of warfare. Grants a large amount of Attack, Magic and Ranged XP.
item_821.lead: Tome of the Dragon Slayer is one of the rewards from completing the main quest, Dragon Slayer.

item_822.desc: Grants a large amount of Attack, Magic and Ranged XP.
item_822.lead: The Tome of the Undying is one of the rewards from completing the main quest, Withering Heights.

item_823.desc: A powerful tome containing ancient techniques of warfare. Grants a large amount of experience in the Attack, Magic and Ranged skills.
item_823.lead: The Tome of Volcano is an item given to the player upon opening the Icthlarin's Little Helper reward pack. It gives the player +750 experience in the Attack, Magic, and Ranged skills.

item_824.desc: A book filled with knowledge on how best to chop down trees. Awards a small amount of Woodcutting XP.
item_824.lead: Tome of Woodcutting - Vol 1 is a skill tome that is one of four rewards given after completing the Restless Ghosts quest and is a reward after the Rune Mysteries quest. It can also be received occasionally from chests. When read, the tome gives 100 Woodcutting experience.

item_825.desc: A book filled with knowledge on how best to chop down trees. Awards a decent amount of Woodcutting XP.
item_825.lead: Tome of Woodcutting - Vol 2 is a skill tome found in chests within Fellhollow. When read, the tome gives 400 Woodcutting experience.

item_826.desc: A garou delicacy, ideal for those night-time munchies.
item_826.lead: Umbral kebab is a consumable food item that provide 80 health and 90 sustenance, as well as the perks Frosted Flavours and Soul Food, which reduces Scorch buildup and restores 8 health every 5 seconds for 300 seconds. It is made with seared cactus steak, bread, roast pumpkin, and steak in a cooking range.

item_827.desc: Made by combining fried grilled undead bass and grilled tomato. Grants the Sea Life perk.
item_827.lead: Undead delight is a consumable food item that provides 180 health and 70 sustenance as well as the perk Sea Life, which restores 3 health every second for 1,200 seconds. It is made with grilled undead bass and grilled tomatoes in a stone range or a cooking range, however a player must interact with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

journal.text: 'Undead Delight' sounds like an audio track from a long-forgotten Halloween event, but NO - it's an unexpectedly tasty meal. The very dead flavours of an undead bass are meshed with the very alive flavours of a tomato, and the combination is capital-D Delicious. We will admit that it's off-putting that the un-alive also find the Undead Delight tasty. Put it in front of a skeleton, zombie, demon or other wretched being and they will gobble it up like there's no tomorrow.

item_828.desc: All of the calories, none of the guilt.
item_828.lead: Vegan fryup is a consumable food item that provides 70 health and 70 sustenance. It is made with baked potato, fried cabbage, and grilled tomatoes in a stone range or a cooking range, however a player must interact with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

journal.text: Crisp and delicious vegetables, neatly fried mushrooms, there are few breakfasts quite as delicious as a fry up, even for those who abjure bacon.

item_829.desc: A tasty soup, good for the soul.
item_829.lead: Vegetable soup is a consumable food item that provides 40 health and 50 sustenance. It is made with fried cabbage and baked potato in a stone range or a cooking range, however a player must interact with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

item_830.desc: A delicious sponge cake, thankfully without the goblin version of frosting.
item_830.lead: Victoria sponge cake is a consumable food item that provides 85 sustenance and 50 health, as well as the perk Sugar Rush, which reduces rest drain by 25% for 300 seconds. It is made with 2 dried redberries, 2 eggs, 2 redberry infusions, and 4 wheat in a stone range or a cooking range after receiving the recipe from the Cook's Assistant quest.

journal.text: Named after Victoria Thistlethwaite, of Bramblemead, this cake has been popular at the most lavish of parties across the region. Victoria was a well-regarded chef, but one whose culinary obsessions lay only with the sweetest of treats. She would craft biscuits, pastries and candied treats of such quality, that even Bandos once visited her little cafe to try one. So moved was the god of war by her delicious pastries, that he left three goblins to watch over her as the war against the garou began, and those goblins would defend her with their lives. Unfortunately, goblin lives are surprisingly fleeting at the best of times, and in an actual war they lasted perhaps no more than a few hours. Victoria's little shop was consumed in a terrible inferno, reducing all her sweetest of treats to little more then motes of blackened ash, whisked away in the wind. In honour of Bandos, and the bond that was struck with this mortal chef, goblins of Ashenfall pass down this cake recipe from generation to generation, in the hope that all might share in the deliciousness.

journal.text: This potion helps you sleep all night and work all day. It gives you the feeling of well oiled elbow and shoulder joints, and it numbs the pain in your muscles from swinging an axe for long stretches at a time.

item_844.desc: PERK: Quarrymaster REDUCES the STAMINA cost of Mining by 33%
item_844.lead: Weak Quarrymaster potion grants the perk Quarrymaster, which reduces the stamina cost of Mining by 33% for 5 minutes (300 seconds). It is made with harralander, clay, and clay vessel in a brewing cauldron.

journal.text: Mining is a strenuous task. Each swing of that pickaxe makes your muscles ache and your bones quiver. Exhaustion creeps into your soul and takes root, making it take longer and longer to gather that precious ore. This potion acts as a pick-me-up. An energizing drink that makes you a monster of a miner, able to swing your pickaxe as though it barely weighs anything at all.

item_845.desc: Pointy! Used to craft Barbed Arrows or to coat your equipped melee weapon with barbs that cause Bleed buildup for a short duration.
item_845.lead: Weapon barbs are an item unlocked at level 22 Ranged, allowing players to either craft barbed arrows or imbue their held melee weapon (except for basic tools such as axes or pickaxes) with the Bleed debuff for two minutes.

journal.text: Used to craft Barbed Arrows or to coat your equipped melee weapon with barbs, causing Bleed buildup for a short duration. Sometimes, you just really want to hurt something. It happens. We each have that little voice that tells us to make something bleed, just a little. Well, blacksmiths thought to themselves, "what if we listen to that voice?" and created these little doohickies. Barbs for your weapons, so that they may tear, rend and otherwise force your opponents to bleed with every strike.

item_846.desc: A vial of Weapon Poison. Used in crafting Poison Arrows or to coat your equipped Melee Weapon with Poison for a short time.
item_846.lead: Weapon poison is a potion that can be created at level 15 Ranged. This allows the player to poison their weapon (excluding tools such as pickaxes or logging axes), making their melee weapon or ranged ammunition poisonous for two minutes.

journal.text: Used in crafting Poison Arrows or to coat your equipped Melee Weapon with Poison for a short time. There are times in life where you really want someone to regret ever meeting you. It could be a long-held grudge, it could be on the battlefield, or it could be in a never-ending meeting that could so easily have been an email but has now persisted past your lunchbreak and you had so been looking forward to that sushi… ahem… sorry, where was I? Oh, yes, pain! Poison is sometimes considered to be a coward’s weapon. Personally, I prefer to think of it as the smart weapon choice, after all, honour is only worth anything if you’re the winner of the battle. A corpse with honour still rots in the dirt. With a blade coated in poison, you can almost guarantee the death of your enemies, all it takes is a single nick and their fate is sealed. An investment well worth making, if you ask me.

item_847.desc: Use this to hone your equipped melee weapon.
item_847.lead: A whetstone can be used to give a 15% damage multiplier on a player's equipped melee weapon for 10 minutes, and can be used in conjunction with damage-boosting spells, such as Enchant Weapon: Fire. Its recipe is unlocked after reaching level 40 in the Attack skill.

journal.text: The blade is not just a weapon in the wilds of Ashenfall, it’s a tool. Sometimes it’s the difference between seeing tomorrow and having a very bad today. Dwarves have always understood the importance of properly maintaining one’s equipment. They turned the care for their weapons into a ritual of almost religious significance. Blades would be cleaned, serviced and sharpened so that they might cut through deadlier dangers and challenge greater threats. The whetstone is a simple device, but one that served as a backbone of this ritual. A smith would learn to gently sharpen the blade to the thinnest edge possible, treating it almost like a competition. They would boast and brag with each other about the sharpness of their blades. A popular dwarven myth speaks of the Prime Whetstone, capable of sharpening a blade to the point that no armour or metal could withstand it. Sadly, or perhaps thankfully, no evidence exists to provide any truth to the myth.

item_848.desc: A triumph of man over nature.
item_848.lead: Wild pie is a consumable food item that provides 90 health, 110 sustenance as well as the perks Knowledgable Nourishment and Grounded, which increases experience gain in all skills by 10%, and reduces the amount of shock damage taken for 600 seconds. It is made with fried onions, baked potato, dried dwellberries, and bread in a cooking range and learned by unlocking Adept Culinaromancer at level 36 Cooking.

journal.text: A delicious pastry crust seals the flavours inside. Warm and filling, each bite designed to fill you with comfort. The flavour is earthy, and rich, letting you shrug off almost anything.

item_866.desc: A key to a specific Nightmare Crucible.
item_866.lead: The crucible engram of betrayal is an item that you can receive after slaying several mini-bosses. The item is used to enter the Nightmare Crucible

journal.text: The mind is a powerful thing. Thought can shape reality; intention turns to impulse, which moves muscle and bone, which in turn can shatter stone. The Aughra were fascinated by such power and sought more and more ways to harness it. For Avisk, who was determined to force his will on all living beings, it was a myriad collection of tools in one, squishy, vessel. Dreams and nightmares were an especially fascinating study. Dreams, like thoughts, can shape reality. A child dreams of the stars and goes in search of the tallest trees, the highest mountains, anything to help him get closer to those twinkling baubles. The elderly dream of their youth and regret decisions made decades in the past. Entire lifespans can exist in moments. Avisk yearned to harness that power. When he crafted the crucibles, he distilled nightmares down to their purest forms. Each one forged from archetypes shared across countless species. Yet what nightmare is stronger then when friends become foes, when trust turns to betrayal. When we look into the eyes of our loved ones, what if it’s hatred that shines back? This key is the concept of betrayal crystallised down and used to unlock the Nightmare Crucible. The beasts inside offer no loyalty, for in a world forged by betrayal they know that trust is nothing but a pleasant fiction.

item_867.desc: A key to a specific Nightmare Crucible.
item_867.lead: The crucible engram of helplessness is an item that you can receive after slaying several mini-bosses. The item is used to enter the Nightmare Crucible

journal.text: The dragonkin Avisk was obsessed with dreams. He believed they were the key to unlocking the true power of the mind. Nightmares, especially, fascinated him. In the folds of a dream he placed powerful creatures in the hope that the dream would infect them, somehow, making them easier for him to possess. He forged each of the crucibles after an archetype of nightmares, strengthening them with the power of the collective unconscious from a variety of species. A rare dragonkin that considered the minds of others races, not just his own. A common nightmare is that feeling of helplessness. That no matter what you do, no matter how hard you try, you are destined to failure. A nightmare so powerful that it seeps into the waking world, inflicting people with imposter syndromes, paranoia and jealousy. This key is that feeling crystallised and used to shape the Nightmare Crucible. Alas the creatures within are not quite as helpless as Avisk hoped.

item_868.desc: A key to a specific Nightmare Crucible.
item_868.lead: The crucible engram of humiliation is an item that you can receive after slaying several mini-bosses. The item is used to enter the Nightmare Crucible

journal.text: Of all the Nightmares that Avisk created, this one came the easiest. It is forged from countless dreams harvested from around the world, of forgetting clothes to class, or saying the exact wrong thing at the exact worst time. Some of this power is because these sorts of embarrassing nightmares can manifest in the real world, all too often, as the human race, in particular, is easily given to shame and regret. The beasts that dwell within the Nightmare Crucible attuned to this particular archetype, are filled with rage. Anger at being forced to relive their most humiliating moments, again and again and again, all as part of the dragonkin’s twisted experiments. When you use this key, and brave this particular nightmare, be sure not to empower it further with your own failure.

item_869.desc: A key to a specific Nightmare Crucible.
item_869.lead: The crucible engram of the hounded is an item that you can receive after slaying several mini-bosses. The item is used to enter the Nightmare Crucible

journal.text: Nightmares are primal fears personified and no fear is so primal as the fear of being hunted. To be chased by some terror, beast or other, that seeks to do us harm. In these dreams our limbs betray us, physics works against us and no matter how hard we try, how fast we run, the monster behind us will always catch up. Avisk knew this and used this primal fear to craft the first Nightmare Crucible. He took the primal fear of every living being, and wove it into a web that would contain the creatures he sought to study. This key is that that fear solidified, and you need only be brave enough to assume the role of the hunter, not the prey.

item_1042.desc: The ancient remnants of some sort of armour. Perhaps you could learn something from it.
item_1042.lead: Tastefully torn tights is a power level 5 vestige that can be purchased with 350 soul fragments at Death's Exchange. Players will need to study this to receive the recipe for the ranger tights.

item_1043.desc: The tattered pieces of a mysterious object. Perhaps you could learn something from them.
item_1043.lead: The tattered time-lost cloth is a vestige that is dropped by skeletal marauders and rotsworn marauders. Upon studying the vestige, players can create the shadowscale cape.

item_1044.desc: Perhaps you could learn from it
item_1044.lead: The Twtiching Antenna is a vestige that unlocks the kalphite carapace helmet.

item_1045.desc: You can feel it pulling away from you. Perhaps you could learn from it.
item_1045.lead: The weighted training band is a consumable item that unlocks creation of the amulet of strength.

item_1046.desc: The remnants of a Zamorakian mage robe. Perhaps you could learn something from it.
item_1046.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_1046.lead: The whispering elbow pad is a vestige that unlocks the Zamorak robes. It is obtained through Evil Emporium for 400 infernal fragments.

item_1047.desc: Perhaps you could learn something from it.
item_1047.lead: The white memory of Menaphos is a vestige that unlocks the white desert cape and can be found in chests throughout Umbral Sands.

item_1048.desc: The remnants of Zamorakian mage robe legs. Perhaps you could learn something from it.
item_1048.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_1048.lead: The wizard's kneecap is a vestige that unlocks the Zamorak robe legs. It is obtained through Evil Emporium for 300 infernal fragments.

item_1049.desc: Perhaps you could learn something from it.
item_1049.lead: The yellow memory of Menaphos is a vestige that unlocks the yellow desert cape and can be found in chests throughout Umbral Sands.

item_1050.desc: The sinister remnants of an abyssal creature.
item_1050.lead: Abyssal ashes are dropped from killing the abyssal demon. They currently have no use.

journal.text: The remnants of an abyssal demon. Fine ashes, infused with malice. Not great for the skin, despite what Doric will tell you.

item_1051.desc: The spine from a deceased abyssal demon.
item_1051.lead: Abyssal spines are dropped from killing the abyssal demon and are a key material for players wishing to craft the abyssal whip. Players will need to bring this abyssal spine to a Dragonkin effigy at the Kletterbuja Kara vault in Bloodblight Swamp to receive the recipe to create the abyssal whip.

journal.text: The spinal column of an abyssal demon. A monstrous creature from between the gaps in reality. It pulses with hatred, and you’re convinced it wriggles occasionally.

item_1052.desc: A resilient adhesive that can withstand high temperatures.
item_1052.lead: Acrid adhesive is a basic item processed from kalphite ichor at the kiln.

journal.text: Please, for the love of the River Goddess, don't lick, sniff or apply acrid adhesive to your skin. You might think it would be worse for the Moon Garou who are covered in fur, but at least they can shed the fur when gets sticky. Its harder to shed a finger or lip.

item_1053.desc: A sturdy metal used for crafting weapons and armour.
item_1053.lead: Adamant bars are a processed material created with three adamantite ore and three coal inside a blast furnace.

journal.text: Adamantite is one of the most durable and impressive metals, that would have revolutionised the human populace of Ashenfall if they’d survived long enough to find it. The Moon Garou have learned to make good use of it, but they are comparatively few in number and have little desire for the industrialisation such metals could bring.

item_1054.desc: A pair of adamant crossbow limbs. Used in crafting a adamant crossbow.
item_1054.lead: Adamant crossbow limbs are used for creating a adamant crossbow.

item_1055.desc: Mined from adamantite deposits. It can be smelted into bars at a Blast Furnace.
item_1055.lead: Adamantite ore is a basic Mining material mined from adamantite ore nodes, which can be found all over the Umbral Sands region. Three ores can be smelted along 3 pieces of coal in a blast furnace to produce adamant bars.

journal.text: Smelt this, alongside coal, to create adamant bars. One of the most impressively durable metals available on Ashenfall, adamantite ore is highly prized by the desert-dwelling Moon Garou, who use it in a variety of endeavours.

item_1056.desc: Glue friendly or else I'll take away the glue and then nobody will have any glue to glue with!
item_1056.lead: Adhesive is a product as well as a crafting item. It is created by adding swamp tar to the kiln. Adhesive is made in a one-to-one ratio, with one swamp tar creating one adhesive.

journal.text: Tacky like your great aunt's wardrobe, this sticky substance has a wide range of uses when it comes to crafting.

item_1057.desc: Equippable as ammo when using a magic weapon. A symbol of blustering winds, essential for air-based magic and other spells. Runes are retained if you happen to die.
item_1057.lead: Air runes can be crafted at a rune altar at level 1 Runecrafting or higher, and can deal between 13-22 base damage, along with whatever staves the player equips. Air runes can also be used in spells, such as Windstep, Axtral Projection, Enchant Weapon: Air, Superheat, and Tempest Shield.

journal.text: Rune essence has the unique property of absorbing and transforming ambient magic into something than can be used by even races without a natural magic aptitude, like humans. An Air Rune contains anima that is aligned with the wind itself. A practitioner of magic can take the rune and convert it into a gentle breeze. Or, with enough of them, a gale force wind. Very popular in the summer months.

item_1058.desc: A crystallised mass of amylase enzymes, can be used as a reagent potions.
item_1058.lead: Amylase crystal can be obtained by opening Agility course reward packs. It is used in making stamina potions.

journal.text: Do you really want to know what amylase crystals are? I know this is a journal and you would expect some elaboration, but sometimes a little mystery is best when it comes to alchemical reagents. Ugh, you're still here? Fine. Amylase crystal is a concentrated deposit of saliva. There's no way of sugar-coating it: you're holding some sun-dried spit right here. And just as it does wonders for digestive processes, it's pretty good at breaking down roughage in potion-crafting.

item_1059.desc: Cute little cannibal fish love some anchovy bait. Irresistible to Herring. Increases the catch chance of this fish.
item_1059.lead: Anchovy bait is a power level 3 Fishing bait crafted at the crafting table. It increases the chance of catching herring. Players can store the bait in a tackle box, which holds up to 48 baits.

journal.text: To attract fish with a taste for saltier prey, there’s little better than a nice anchovy strung up and offered as a sacrifice to those that dwell beneath the waves.

item_1060.desc: Tree bark infused with magical energy.
item_1060.lead: Anima-infused bark is a basic crafting item that is required to create wild anima. Anima bark can be found on the ground around the anima trees and certain crystal trees located throughout the Fractured Plains biome. Players can interact with the item by picking it up, receiving 7 Woodcutting experience. Anima-infused bark can respawn after 72 minutes. [[File:Anima Tree.png|300px|thumb|A anima tree with Anima-infused bark found on the ground around the tree.]] [[File:Anima-Infused Bark (item, placed).png|thumb|right|Anima-infused bark on the ground.]]

journal.text: The magic of Ashenfall permeates the very trees of the region, imbuing their bark with mystical properties. This bark can be refined into wild anima, a magical crafting component that is popular with spellcasters of all kinds.

item_1061.desc: A sturdy bone from a sizable creature.
item_1061.lead: Animal bones are retrieved from killing animals such as cows, deer, and sheep. They can also be found on the ground in a cave in the Stormtouched Highlands. Players can also receive it by casting Bark To Bones on a tree. Upon receiving a bone for the first time, players can unlock the tannery and the stone range.

journal.text: Bones are not just the favoured materials of necromancers, they can be incredibly useful to a skilled survivalist as well. Designed to withstand great force, while still being as light as possible, bones make excellent components in an array of crafting recipes.

item_1062.desc: Gathered from big creatures, this hide is essential for crafting leather equipment.
item_1062.lead: Animal hide is a basic item gathered from animals like cows, deer, and wolves. It can be put into the tannery to create leather.

item_1063.desc: Gathered from small creatures, too small to be processed into leather by itself.
item_1063.lead: Animal hide scraps are gathered from rats, kebbits, and chinchompas to create leather.

item_1064.desc: To a fish, this feather looks like a long-lost love. Makes Armoured Catfish enamoured. Increases the catch chance of this fish.
item_1064.lead: Animated feathers are a power level 6 Fishing bait crafted at the crafting table. It increases the chance of catching armoured catfish. Players can store the bait in a tackle box, which holds up to 48 baits.

journal.text: When sparkly feathers coated in delicious juice are not enough, then create one that dances. The animated feather is infused with magic and when it reaches the water it writhes and wriggles in a hypnotic dance that fish feel mystically drawn to. If you hang one from a window, you may also find other weak-minded creatures dancing to its mysterious movements. Like Terry. Terry is an idiot.

item_1065.desc: A cartilaginous extension of a deer skull.
item_1065.lead: Antlers are obtained by killing deer and are used in drinks, weapons, and armour.

item_1074.desc: Pieces of wood collected from branches, saplings and Ash trees.
item_1074.lead: Ash logs are obtained by chopping down ash trees, picking them up off the ground, uprooting saplings, or chopping down thorny vines.

item_1075.lead: Ash planks are made by using ash logs on a sawmill. Ash planks can be used for construction or as an alternative to creating charcoal.

item_1077.desc: Astral runes are used for casting advanced magic spells and attacks. Runes are retained if you happen to die.
item_1077.lead: Astral runes can be crafted at a rune altar at level 3 Runecrafting or higher. Astral runes are used in enchanting weapons, finding/gathering resources easily, accessing chests, and providing shelter.

item_1078.lead: Avantoe is an herb obtained by harvesting Avantoe plants. It can be farmed by planting avantoe seeds in a willow farming plot, with iron secateurs providing an increased yield when harvesting.

journal.text: Everything about the avantoe is quickfire. It grows quickly, blooms fast, and is a superb catalyst, reacting quickly in potion-making. It's a plant in a rush, eager to germinate and get the next avantoe on its way. Meanwhile, I can spend an hour trying to work out what to eat today, and can stare at an empty space where a journal should be for even longer.

item_1079.desc: Cultivated grains ground to a fine powder.
item_1079.lead: Bag of flour is a power level 2 processed material, which means it can be cooked at a kiln into bread starting at Cooking Level 12, and not burnt into burnt bread at level 27. It can be grinded from wheat with a grindstone.

item_1080.desc: A Barrel Cactus seed. Pop it into a farming plot and start growing! Best planted in Umbral Sand plots.
item_1080.lead: Barrel cactus seeds are a type of Umbral Sands Seed, used in the Farming skill. Barrel cactus seeds can be used to grow Barrel Cactus (Farming) in a farming plot. However, it is best to plant them in a yew farming plot.

journal.text: We doff our caps to you. You walked into Umbral Sands from Dowdun Reach, looked at the sands, scorch and giant dragon and thought "you know what? I'm going to do some farming". You're as based as the people who, likewise, were confronted by all of those things and promptly built a giant wooden house. Of all the things to grow, we can actually understand the barrel cactus. Native to this region, it's also full of moisture – thus the 'barrel' – which is reasonably integral to the game you are playing."

item_1081.desc: A tasty mushroom. Can be used in a variety of cooking recipes.
item_1081.lead: Bittercap mushrooms are a power level 2 raw ingredient, which means they can be cooked at a campfire or grill into grilled mushrooms starting at Cooking Level 12, and not burnt into burnt mushroom at level 27. They can also be used to make weak antipoison potion. They can be gathered from bittercap mushroom (plant)s in the Whispering Swamp and Dowdun Reach.

item_1082.desc: A pair of Black crossbow limbs. Used in crafting a Black Knight Crossbow.
item_1082.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_1082.lead: Black crossbow limbs are a component in creating the shadow crossbow. They are created at a blacksmith's bench.

journal.text: Did you know that someone who fires a crossbow is often considered an 'arbalister' or 'arbalist'? Don't say that these journals don't teach you something.

item_1083.desc: A bar of reforged black metal scraps. Used to make Black Knight gear.
item_1083.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_1083.lead: An black metal bar is a component of a variety of armour and weapons.

item_1084.desc: Dropped from Black Knights. Can be reforged into black metal at a Blast Furnace.
item_1084.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_1084.lead: Black metal scraps is dropped from Black Knights. Six scraps can be combined with three coal in a blast furnace to create one black metal bar. Alternatively, players can create different coloured chandeliers and torches.

journal.text: Fun fact: black metal is actually steel that has gone through a form of vulcanisation. Demonic or draconic sulphur are used in the process, to slightly different effect. Demonic vulcanisation gives the metal a matte finish, while draconic is more chromatic. What you have here is some scraps of black metal. Could be demonic, could be draconic. They're likely off-cuts from the smithing or vulcanisation process, or it's entierly possible that they were bashed off a Black Knight's armour when you boffed them. Regardless, waste not, want not. Now you have the material required for some new gear.

item_1085.desc: Scraps that can be searched through. Little bits of Black Knight are in there.
item_1085.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_1085.lead: Black salvage piles are drops from defeating Black Knights. Nine salvage piles can be combined with three coal in a blast furnace, to create one black metal bar.

item_1086.desc: Logs cut from ancient trees or roots.
item_1086.lead: Blightwood can be found in Bloodblight Swamp. The wood can be chopped from the pale roots on larger trees in the swamp.

journal.text: There is something about the swamps of Ashenfall that encourage strange trees to grow. The result is Blightwood; durable, powerful and somehow capable of channelling more potent magic than other trees. The Wild Knights joked that Blightwood houses the souls of the victims of the swamp, and that they are imbued with their regrets and hatred. It's probably not true. Probably.

item_1087.desc: Harvested from bloodwood trees found in the toxic swamp in Ghornfell.
item_1087.lead: Bloodwood sap can be found by logging the red formations on the bloodwood tree in the southernmost area of the Bloodblight Swamp, that is located in the middle of a garou camp.

item_1088.desc: Obtained from felled Lesser Blue Dragons. Can be processed at the tannery.
item_1088.lead: Blue dragon hide is a basic material dropped by blue dragons which can be tanned to create blue dragonhide leather.

journal.text: Blacksmiths hate this one simple trick. They spend their lives mastering interlocking chains and plates, only for dragons to be born with them. A third of the blacksmith's punters are now gone, hunting for dragons rather than dropping some coin at their forges. It's enough to make a blacksmith sob into their anvil. Blue dragons hate this one simple trick too, of course. Their Venn diagram overlaps with the blacksmith's: they'd rather people got their armour from somewhere other than dragons.

item_1089.desc: Made by tanning blue dragonhide. A key component for ranged armour.
item_1089.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_1089.lead: Blue dragon leather is a processed material created from tanning blue dragon hide.

item_1090.desc: Obtained from felled lesser blue dragons. Can be ground into blue dragon dust.
item_1090.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_1090.lead: Blue dragon scale is dropped from blue dragon. One scale can be ground into two blue dragon scale dust.

journal.text: There is a curious trend in Gielinor, whereby the most fragile fighters - archers and magic users - are easiest to spot. From blue dragonhide to mystic robes, the fashion is to wear garish colours, as if the rules of the animal kingdom apply. But no, archers and magic users aren't poisonous, venomous or hoping to be mistaken for a bee. We wonder why that lack of subtlety might be. In the case of blue dragons and their scales, perhaps it's a cruel joke played by the dragonkin. They have been seen that humans keep killing their creations, wearing their hides as trophies. They've got their revenge by way of generous use of the rainbow.

item_1091.desc: Ground from blue dragon scales. Integral to making antifire potions.
item_1091.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_1091.lead: Blue dragon scale dust is a processed material used to make antifire potions.

journal.text: Blue dragon dust is one of those things where you wonder who invented it, and what curious sequence of events led to it happening. Some unknown person had the wherewithal to strip a dragon of dragon scales, crush those scales in a pestle and mortar, then apply the resulting dust to a potion. Not only that, they downed said potion and stood in the path of a dragon. Does that not seem inexorably mad to you? But thank you, inexorably mad person, because now we have this potent ingredient which can protect a person from dragonfire. You have been forgotten in time, but your blue dusty legacy lives on.

item_1092.desc: A rare bar of refined blurite, thought to be a myth.
item_1092.lead: A blurite bar can be made in a furnace by smelting three blurite ore. This bar is used in the smithing anvil to create blurite limbs for a blurite crossbow and make the blurite bolts in the fletching bench.

item_1093.desc: A pair of blurite crossbow limbs. Used in crafting a Blurite Crossbow.
item_1093.lead: Blurite crossbow limbs are used in crafting blurite crossbows. They are crafted at a blacksmith's bench after unlocking the recipe with the vestige: azure metal contraption.

journal.text: Not all cats are terrified of crossbows, though most of the Bramblemead population quickly learned to fear them. Some cats could see their merit but were painfully aware of their human pet’s limited imagination. Mittens was the lifelong owner of Gothren Actillian. A blacksmith’s cat, he had learned how to keep the forge fires perfectly hot by playfully jumping on the bellows periodically – something his pet seemed to enjoy. He knew the right length of time a sword should be cooled for and would make sure his human stuck to that timing by offering useful alarms made of glorious clattering things. But blurite? That was a new one. Mittens could see there was little value to the metal, beyond some weird human aesthetic that he did not understand, yet there was some potential to the construction. With carefully timed meows, and some creative knocking over of reagents, Mittens was able to engineer a crossbow of superior design, worthy of his cherished pet.

item_1094.desc: A chunk of rare and unrefined blurite.
item_1094.lead: Blurite ore is a basic Mining material found by mining the blurite ore nodes in the Takla Kara vault. Players can smelt this ore in a furnace to make blurite bars.

journal.text: Sometimes colours just want to manifest themsleves. There is the sweetness of orange. The cowardice of yellow, and the peaceful serenity of a summery green. Blue, tired of being linked to only sorrow and sadness, sought a physical existence. One that could be shaped into new and wonderous things, and so blurite was born. A metal that is so very, very, blue. It's in the name. After all, it's blue, right?

item_1095.desc: Crossbow limbs made from powerful bone. Used in crafting the Dorgeshuun Crossbow.
item_1095.lead: Bone crossbow limbs can be created at a blacksmith's bench and can be used to craft a Dorgeshuun crossbow.

journal.text: Following certain incidents with cats and crossbow limbs, a superstition began to build in Bramblemead about the danger of crossbows and felines. It was considered bad luck to house a cat in the same home as a crossbow, with reasoning ranging from the safety of the cat, to the safety of the human population should cats rise up and develop opposable thumbs. While harmless at first, as the conflict with the garou grew the need for crossbows, cats found themselves with fewer and fewer homes willing to house them. Over the years, this led to domestic cats becoming a rare sight in Bramblemead. It also created a deep-seated resentment among cats, and they plotted their revenge. Most would tell you that cats had nothing to do with the destruction of Bramblemead and the Brynmoor settlements. Yet, if you ask a cat, they will simply purr with a sinister grin.

item_1096.desc: A versatile crafting material, smelted from bars of copper and tin.
item_1096.lead: A bronze bar is a material used to craft weapons and armour. It is created by smelting 3 copper ore and 3 tin ore at a furnace. Receiving the bronze bar in the player's inventory will unlock the following:

journal.text: An ingot of a copper-tin alloy. Highly prized by blacksmiths.

item_1097.desc: A pair of bronze crossbow limbs. Used in crafting a Bronze Crossbow.
item_1097.lead: Bronze crossbow limbs are used in crafting bronze crossbows. They are crafted at a blacksmith's bench.

journal.text: The complicated mechanisms of the crossbow sparked a small technological revolution in Bramblemead. Such devices had once been the domain of the dwarves, who guarded their advanced techniques to maintain their smithing dominion. However, soon human smiths found themselves creating these complex trigger mechanisms. There were casualties, certainly. Some mechanisms tightened strings too greatly, snapping back with a force that could cause serious harm. One notable example involved the pet belonging to the village priest, a curious feline with absolutely no sense of self-preservation. The cat entered the workshop, as she so often did, and took it upon herself to knock everything she could to the floor. Unfortunately, in doing so, she triggered the release mechanism being worked on and quickly learned that cats are not meant to fly.

item_1098.desc: A thin sheet of purest bronze, can be used for demonstrating your prowess, potion making or even recycling into bronze bars.
item_1098.lead: Bronze leaves are a craftable item reward from various Agility courses that allows the player to make potions or create bronze bars. To obtain these, players must either collect them from bronze (or better) reward packs or recycle bronze bars in the jeweler's bench to make sheets of ten per bar.

journal.text: If you want to prettify some jewellery or clothing, there's nothing quite like leaf filigree. It makes you realise that nature really knows what it is doing. Everywhere you look, we've embellished our craftmanship{{sic|incorrectly spelled "craftsmanship"

item_1099.desc: Scraps that can be searched through. Seems like it's just a pile of bronze offcuts.
item_1099.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_1099.lead: Bronze salvage piles are a basic material, nine of them can be smelted in a furnace to create one bronze bar.

item_1100.desc: A Bunny Cactus seed. Pop it into a farming plot and start growing! Best planted in Umbral Sand plots.
item_1100.lead: Bunny cactus seeds are a type of Umbral Sand seed, used in the Farming skill. Bunny cactus seeds can be used to grow Bunny Cactus (Farming) in a farming plot. However, it is best to plant them in a yew farming plot.

journal.text: The bunny cactus isn't only named that way because of its rabbit-ear-like limbs. It's also a prolific reproducer. A single plant can produce dozens of seeds, and in turn it can create dozens of bunny cacti. Now I think of it, the bunny cactus also develops little tufts of fur on its spikes, reminiscent of a rabbit's cotton tail. Damn, they really nailed the naming of this cactus.

item_1101.lead: Cabbages are a power level 2 raw ingredient, which means they can be cooked at a campfire or grill into fried cabbage starting at Cooking Level 12, and not burnt into burnt cabbage at level 27. They can also be used to make weak Focused Cooking potions and Focused Cooking potions. They can be gathered from cabbage plants in Bramblemead Valley and cabbage (Farming) from cabbage seeds.

item_1102.desc: Cabbage Seeds. Equip and use them to scatter these into a farming plot and start growing! Best Planted in Brynmoor plots.
item_1102.lead: Cabbage seeds are a type of Brynmoor seed, used in the Farming skill. Cabbage seeds can be used to grow Cabbage in a farming plot. However, it is best to plant them in ash farming plot.

journal.text: Hail Brassica Prime, lord of deliciousness and nutrition! Within these tiny seeds rest all the power of creation, ready to burst forth into spherical orbs of crisp deliciousness. Guthix once encountered Brassica Prime when he wandered the moors of Ashenfall. On a strange outcrop, beneath a waterfall that reflected the silver moonlight, he spied a cabbage so large and so full of nutrition that he was briefly stunned at its magnificence. When the cabbage spoke, the god of balance found himself quite at a loss. According to the cabbage, he was the lord of all vegetables, and keeper of the ancient secrets of a balanced diet, seeing some small kinship in Guthix's search for harmony. They held long and curious conversations, deep into the night, about the nature of magic, divinity and, of course, food. Brassica's stories changed every night. Each moonrise offered a new excuse for his divinity, and new lessons on how he had supposedly shaped creation itself, by mixing together the base vitamins needed for the universe to thrive. Mad, perhaps, or just composed of an alien way of thinking, but Guthix took some small comfort in his strange new friend. As such, he made a point of having his druids sow cabbage seeds in every field and around all his settlements, so that Brassica might be honoured in some small way

item_1103.lead: Cactus fibres is a material item created at a tannery, and is a requirement to make desert cloth.

journal.text: Not all cacti deserve to live. Some need to be culled in case they join the trees' campaign against humanity. Fortunately, these plant-base anarchists can be refined into useful fibres that can help with crafting.

item_1104.desc: A moist and sweet botanical edible. It has a fresh floral fragrance.
item_1104.lead: Cactus steak is a power level 5 raw ingredient.

item_1105.desc: A handful of Cadavaberry Seeds. Equip and use them to scatter these into a farming plot and start growing! Best planted in Fellhollow plots.
item_1105.lead: Cadavaberry seeds are a type of Fellhollow seed, used in the Farming skill. Cadavaberry seeds can be obtained from harvesting wild cadavaberry bushes.

journal.text: Sometimes you just want to fill your garden wth deadly berries. This was certainly true of Agnes DeWithlington-Smithe, a self-proclaimed "witch" with zero magical talent. She delighted in filling her garden with strange and dangerous herbs and flowers. The more poisonous, the better. Locals would claim that she was a retired assassin, trying to hone her craft. In truth, she just discovered something about the plants that she admired and, ultimately, she thought they were pretty.

item_1106.desc: Produced by burning wood in a kiln. Charcoal is a very efficient fuel.
item_1106.lead: Charcoal is a form of fuel created by processing wood at a kiln. Charcoal provides facilities 3 minutes of fuel time, serving as an improvement over using wood as a fuel source. In addition to being a fuel source, charcoal is a reagent for other items and buildings.

item_1107.desc: Essential for pottery and construction, dig it up from nearby water sources.
item_1107.lead: Clay is a basic Mining material that can be mined from clay nodes. It can be used at a pottery wheel to craft a variety of items, which must then be fired using a kiln. Note that clay can be worked directly, and does not need to be made into soft clay.

journal.text: This sticky brown substance is rarely considered the right answer to the classic joke. However, it has many more uses outside the realm of low-tier comedy.

item_1108.desc: A figurine made of clay. Now hardened.
item_1108.lead: A clay decoration is an item that can be crafted by using three pieces of clay on a pottery wheel to produce a clay decoration (unfired), and then using the unfired clay decoration on a kiln to create the finished clay decoration.

item_1109.desc: A figurine made of clay. Still wet.
item_1109.lead: Clay decoration (unfired) is an item that is unlocked after mining and receiving clay for the first time. Players can fire the clay with a kiln, creating a fired clay decoration.

item_1110.desc: A blank canvas for creating enchanted amulets; just add precious metals and gems.
item_1110.lead: A clay mould is a clay mould that is fired in a kiln and is used as an ingredient at the jeweler's bench for making trinkets.

item_1111.desc: Bake this in a kiln to create an amulet mould.
item_1111.lead: An unfired clay mould is a resource that is created by combining three clay on a pottery wheel. It can be fired at a kiln to create a clay mould.

item_1112.lead: Clay vessels can be created with clay vessel (unfired) at a kiln, and can be used at a brewing cauldron to hold potions.

item_1113.desc: A formed clay bowl, ready to be fired in a kiln.
item_1113.lead: A clay vessel (unfired) can be created with clay at a pottery wheel. Can be fired using a kiln to make a clay vessel.

item_1114.desc: Typically found in rocky areas and caves. Combine with metal ores at an upgraded smelter to create higher tiered metal bars.
item_1114.lead: Coal is a basic Mining material mined from coal nodes, which can be found all over the Fellhollow, Dowdun Reach and Umbral Sands regions. It is used as a secondary ingredient for ores smelted in a blast furnace.

journal.text: Coal is the petrified memory of a long dead ecosystem. Plants and animals that lived countless aeons ago, crushed down into rocks of rigid carbon to become a powerful fuel that changes civilisations. When you burn the coal, imagine the worlds that came before and the lives forgotten. Let each piece become a funeral pyre for a long-lost age. Or enjoy shiny new steel armour, your call!

item_1115.desc: It's not much, but it'll keep you warm. Required to craft a basic bed.
item_1115.lead: Coarse animal fur is a basic item gathered from killing kebbits and rats. Players can also receive 1-2 furs from bird nests. Players who receive coarse animal fur in their inventory for the first time unlocks the creation of the bedroll.

journal.text: Bundles of animal fur, scratchy and thick. While not an ideal trait on pets, this sort of coarse fur has a multitude of uses in the wild.

item_1116.desc: Spun from flax at a Spinning Wheel.
