Runes were ground down and mixed with plant oils to create a special resin that allowed the Wild Knights to work their magic through the bow, as if they were carrying runes. That magic has faded and the recipe for the mixture is lost to the ages, but these bows are still formidable in their own right. Wild Knights told tales of creatures that lived within the wilds of Ashenfall and that could not be felled by normal bows. Deer with hides that glistened with starlight, sheep with silver fleeces repelled all arrows. They claimed that these magically infused bows were the only ones capable of harming the creatures, though none ever returned with trophies to share.

item_1524.desc: An agile Longbow crafted from Willow.
item_1524.lead: The willow longbow is a power level 5 longbow that can be crafted from a fletching bench.

journal.text: Ulv had many skills, but hunting was his strongest. He was inherently quiet, still as the night, and he could hold his position, in the trees or bushes, for hours at a time. Ravanna was never good at this. When the two of them hunted together, Ravanna would sneeze, cough, or scream at the sight of an unexpected insect, and the two of them would watch their quarry disappear off into the night. Although this would occasionally test their friendship, Ulv never really held it against Ravanna. Instead, he continued attempting to teach the necromancer the ways of the forest, and the techniques the Wild Knights would use to track down game. It never took. Try as she might, Ravanna was never going to be silent as a shadow. In apology, she looked for a way to create a weapon that would reduce the impact of her noisy nature. Longbows fired further and faster, meaning that less stealth was needed. She made her way into Fellhollow in search of a material strong enough, and returned with willow branches that she crafted into a longbow as a gift for her friend. Their hunts improved dramatically afterward. That was, until they became the hunted.

item_1525.desc: A professional-looking fishing rod, effective in Fellhollow.
item_1525.lead: The willow rod is a power level 5 Fishing tool crafted at the blacksmith's bench.

journal.text: The weeping willow is a sallow tree, known for its love of water. Find a brook or ford and a willow will be there, lost in its reflection. That familiarity with water makes willow a strong wood for fishing rods. There's the merest wisp of magic running through it, an affinity for water. The fish recognise that affinity and relax. They circle until they're caught, which is pretty handy for an angler.

item_1526.desc: An agile Shortbow crafted from Willow.
item_1526.lead: The willow shortbow is a power level 5 Shortbow that can be crafted at a fletching bench.

journal.text: As the dead rose in greater and greater numbers, the villagers needed stronger weapons to defeat them. Their ash and oak longbows failed to unleash sufficient force needed to stem the relentless tide of the undead. They needed a stronger material, that was also flexible enough to deliver arrows of great enough force. Willow was their solution. It is said that the first willow shortbow was gifted to a villager by a spirit that dwelled within the grove. Legends say that the spirit had an unnatural beauty, and would lure foolish villagers into the waters where they would be drowned. Yet, somehow, one villager earned not the spirits ire, but their admiration. The spirit gave up their immortal life, to court the villager. They brought gifts of flowers, fish and finally they gifted a shortbow made from the willow trees in the spirits grove. The validity of this tale is hotly debated, with most assuming it is little more than myth, yet willow groves are still considered spiritual places, where one must be careful who they talk to.

item_1527.desc: A silver dagger that brings fear to all those who howl in the night.
item_1527.lead: The wolfbane dagger is a power level 5 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. The recipe is acquired from a dragonkin effigy found in Vekchenven Kara, the dragonkin vault in central Fellhollow. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.

item_1528.lead: Wooden arrows were proposed to be power level 1 ammunition, crafted at a crafting table. According to the cache, the recipe for making wooden arrows is unlocked after receiving ash logs for the first time. However, the wooden arrows are not in the game; they were just used as an old spell prototype.

item_1529.desc: A basic melee weapon. Handy in a pinch.
item_1529.lead: The wooden club was a power level 1 one-handed mace that is currently not in the game.

journal.text: Sticks and stones may break your bones and this club is proof of the first bit. A large stuck that can be swung with impressive heft, capable of crushing bone with surprising ease. Popular by every warrior ever, when they're abandoned in the woods and need to defend themselves.

item_1530.desc: Basic protection for those seeking to block and parry more efficiently.
item_1530.lead: The wooden shield is a power level 1 shield that can be crafted at a crafting table. [[File:Wooden Shield Block.jpg|thumb|right|a player Blocking with a Wooden Shield]]

journal.text: The children of Bramblemead loved nothing more than to craft themselves wooden shields and swords and then challenge one another to single combat. They would play the roles of brave heroes against dastardly villains, whacking one another with their wooden toys. It kept the local healers busy. Yet, a Wooden Shield is no toy and has saved the lives of countless warriors. As a beast’s claws slice against you, having a hunk of wood between you and the creature is much appreciated. Wood splinters, but flesh bleeds, and blood is less easily replaced than timber.

item_1531.desc: A rudimentary spade made from Ash wood. Used to clear farming plots.
item_1531.lead: A wooden spade is a power level 1 spade that can be crafted at a crafting table. When used to dig a farming plot, players will use 10 stamina and progress by 20% to the next plot clearing stage. Therefore, it will take five digs to progress one stage.

journal.text: Sometimes the very earth itself must be punished for its cruelty! These wooden tools, simple and elegant, can break through the planet's crust, letting you show Gielinor exactly who's boss.

item_1532.desc: Causes damage to their self esteem more than anything really.
item_1532.lead: The wooden training sword is a power level 2 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a crafting table. The recipe is learned by consuming the an educational blade, found in a chest atop the eastern roof of the church in Temple Woods. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.

journal.text: In the village of Bramblemead, children grew up knowing battle. The God Wars hadn't reached them yet, but the priests always knew that danger was coming. So children were taught combat in the form of a game. Carpenters were encouraged to make little wooden swords so that the children could emulate the noble paladins who wandered the village. These soldiers were held up as role models. Young men and women daydreamed through school of taking up those glittering swords and running off into adventure. These weapons clicked and clacked against one another, seemingly harmless to the adults that watched. But wood in Bramblemead was hardened and preserved by druidic magic, and the damage these swords could deal soom became clear. Injuries were common, bruises and broken bones were the rite of passage of every child. It was fortunate, perhaps, that these weapons were so painful — because the children of Bramblemead grew up with a better understanding that war was no game.

item_1533.lead: The wooden watering can is a tool created at the crafting table. It is used to hydrate farming plots and has a capacity of 200 water and has a water rate of 10 per action. The can may be filled with either dirty water or clean water, but not both at the same time. When the can is filled, it may not be filled with the opposite type until it is emptied. Players can empty the can at any time and refill it with a different water type.

journal.text: Rain is unreliable. It is far too whimsical in when and where it falls. Relying on its good nature is a sure-fire way to court drought, famine and ruin. Because of this, the druids created rainfall you could hold, handheld containers of water that could be summoned when and where it was needed. Fill one of these up from any water source and you can use it to keep your farming plots nice and moist.

item_1534.desc: Made with two wool threads at a crafting table. Unwieldy but does the job.
item_1534.lead: The wool net is a power level 3 Fishing tool crafted at the crafting table. It is used to catch shrimp and anchovies from net fishing spots found in Brynmoor and Ghornfell.

journal.text: Wool is absolutely rubbish in water. Throw a sheep in a lake if you don't believe us. The water soaks into the wool and turns the poor animal into a sad, soggy anchor. That rubbishness is - conversely - rather useful when it comes to nets. The wool clods up, leaving barely any holes for a shrimp to make a getaway. It's also heavy as sin. The marine life is thoroughly pinned. Now, getting the water out of the net: that's another matter entirely. You might do well to leave it out to dry in the Umbral Sands.

item_1535.desc: A trusty lightsource - now in yellow.
item_1535.lead: The yellow torch is a cosmetic variation of the torch tool item that can be wielded in the off-hand to help light up areas around the player, making it easier to see. It can be unlocked by studying extinguished yellow remnants.

item_1536.desc: An impactful longbow carved from yew.
item_1536.lead: One hunter, Flytr, was the first to craft a longbow from the yew trees in the oases. Legend had it that the trees were sacred, special, a gift of the River Mother, designed to keep the Moon Garou safe. It was the greatest of blasphemies to use the wood for anything, but Flytr had never been particularly concerned with matters of faith.

journal.text: The hunter is the lifeblood of the Moon Garou. The Umbral Sands are not as hospitable to agriculture as many would like, so diets must be supplemented with fresh meat. This is particularly true for the Moon Garou, who remain primarily carnivorous in nature. One hunter, Flytr, was the first to craft a longbow from the yew trees in the oases. Legend had it that the trees were sacred, special, a gift of the River Mother, designed to keep the Moon Garou safe. It was the greatest of blasphemies to use the wood for anything, but Flytr had never been particularly concerned with matters of faith. She found a tree that had been struck by lightning, to lessen the guilt of repurposing the wood. She whittled down branch and bough, to create the longbow and, when she was done, she could have sworn the weapon was excited to be used. It felled foes at great range, making her one of the best hunters the tribe had ever seen. Soon after, yew trees were no longer protected, as it came to be believed that the strength of the bow was proof that the River Mother wanted the wood to be used.

item_1537.desc: A fishing rod made from yew and adamant.
item_1537.lead: The yew rod is a power level 7 Fishing tool crafted at the blacksmith's bench.

journal.text: For a short period of time, there was an alliance between the trees and sea-dwelling creatures of Ashenfall. They shared common ground, after all: a hatred of being set on fire and chopped, primarily by humans and *spit* adventurers (trees would try to spit, but it mostly led to an unbecoming dribble of sap). The alliance didn't last long, mostly thanks to miscommunication down to a lack of common language. During a gathering at a seashore glade, the fish brought a contingent of hammerheads and sawfish, which the trees deemed overly aggressive. In retaliation, the yew trees 'showed a bit of branch' to a passing angler, and that angler found out that yew made for a spectacular fishing rod. There has been no talk of an alliance since then.

item_1538.desc: A strong shortbow made from yew.
item_1538.lead: Yew shortbow is a power level 7 ranged weapons

journal.text: Moon Garou scouts scour the desert armed with these bows. The sands obscure much until you’re right on top of it and so these bows are often more useful than the longer ranged weapons, against the dangers of the desert. In the camps, the eldest garou will often teach the young cubs how to handle a shortbow. They will have the youngsters unleash a volley of arrows at clay pots, straw dolls, or cacti, and help train them to fire with greater accuracy. Many of the young cubs will keep the shortbow with them as they grow into adulthood, using it as a decorative piece in their home -- a sign of a youth well spent, and a reminder that nothing lasts forever.

item_1539.desc: Standard issue for any mage in Dowdun Reach.
item_1539.update: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
item_1539.lead: The zamorak staff is a power level 6 staff that can be crafted with a mystic forge. This staff and its recipe are unlocked after completing What's Theirs is Mine!, the nodestone quest in Dowdun Reach. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.

item_1540.desc: A zombie's arm with electrifying properties. High five!
item_1540.lead: The zombie arm is a power level 4 melee weapon that is awarded to the player after completing The Great Body Robbery, and can then be crafted using a blacksmith's bench. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.

journal.text: Let us dwell, for a moment, on the original owner of this club, a man named Mort. Mortimer Grimm had the sort of name adored by those who believe in nominative determinism. Mort Grimm, his parents effectively cursed him at birth to become an undead monstrosity, and their curse came true. The undead were rare in Ghornfell, but not unheard of. Some druids, who spent too long in the Whispering Swamps, apparently learned strange rituals that would raise a corpse as a mindless servant, doomed to wander the world in search of delicious, delicious brains. Mort was one of these, though he resurrected with somewhat less all-consuming-hunger than his cohorts. As the other zombies were herded towards human encampments, Mort wandered off into the poisonous Bloodblight Swamp, in search of mysteries. There he encountered a strange scientist who did not immediately attempt to set him on fire – an improvement over the response from most people. This would begin a truer friendship than Mort thought possible. Whilst, yes, the scientist could never remember Mort's name and insisted on calling him Igor. And, yes, Mort would spend much of his time listening to lectures on why everyone else is stupid, whilst carrying large and disturbingly-shaped bags of unknown contents, for the scientist. Still, they would laugh and they would watch the sunsets together, and for the first time in a long time, Mort was happy. Until the scientist asked Mort to build the lightning conductor. One flash of inspiration later, and Mort's tragic existence reduced itself to this somewhat sinister club. Still, waste not want not, I always say.

item_1541.desc: Made in the style of an ancient axe often found in the hands of zombies, it is capable of dealing both Crush and Slash damage at the same time. There seems to be more to this axe though...
item_1541.lead: The zombie axe is a power level 5 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. The axe and its recipe are received by completing Doric's Quest. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.

journal.text: Captain Artorius Flamhanger was a brave man, who stood against the rampaging forces of the damned even as his defences crumbles around him. He never wavered, never faltered, and never left a man behind. In a better world, there would be songs about him. But Fellhollow scorns legacy, leaving only ruins and despair where hope might take root. He held the line against the encroaching horde far longer than anywhere else in the region. Days turned into months and months grew into years. As the rest of the region vanished into death, despair and rot, Captain Flamhanger stood strong. As his children died and rose again, the captain returned them to the earth with sombre compassion. when his wife joined them in death, he gave her a final kiss of polished silver that cleaved her head from her shoulder. In a better world he might have held back the darkness, stood as a single ray of light in a world of shadow. But this is not our world. There are no sages of this man, no great texts telling of his heroic deeds. The only sound he made in the time after his death, is the bubbling song of digestive acids within a zogre's belly. History is penned by the survivors and the victors, yet the deeds of the dead echo across time. This axe, simple as it may appear, is infused with vengeance against the dead that had taken so much from a good man.
